name: St. Mary, Mother of God
facts: Central figure of Christianity; declared Theotokos at Council of Ephesus in 431
Appeared to St. Juan Diego at Guadalupe in 1531
Honored as Mother of God on January 1 since the 1969 liturgical reform
Proclaimed Queen of Heaven by Pope Pius XII in 1954
titleHook: Mother of God & Queen of Heaven

name: St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory Nazianzen
facts: Basil founded the first Eastern monastic rule still used today
Gregory presided over the First Council of Constantinople in 381
Both defended the full divinity of the Holy Spirit against Arianism
Basil built the Basiliad, a complex serving the poor and sick in Caesarea
titleHook: Doctors Who Defended the Trinity

name: St. Genevieve
facts: Led Paris in prayer during Attila the Hun's siege in 451; the city was spared
Became a nun at age 15 after meeting St. Germanus of Auxerre
Her relics were carried in procession during the 1927 flood of Paris
Patroness of Paris for over 1,500 years
titleHook: Patroness Who Saved Paris from Attila

name: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
facts: First native-born American canonized as a saint in 1975
Founded the Sisters of Charity, the first American religious community for women
Converted to Catholicism after her husband's death in Italy in 1803
Established the first free Catholic school for girls in the United States
titleHook: First American-Born Saint

name: St. John Neumann
facts: Fourth Bishop of Philadelphia; spoke eight languages to serve immigrants
Built nearly 100 Catholic schools and 50 churches in his diocese
Introduced the Forty Hours Devotion to the United States in 1853
Canonized in 1977 as the first American bishop saint
titleHook: Bishop Who Built 100 Catholic Schools

name: St. André Bessette
facts: Brother André of Montreal built St. Joseph's Oratory with nickels from the poor
Cured thousands through devotion to St. Joseph and anointing with oil
Worked as a Holy Cross brother and porter for 40 years despite ill health
Canonized in 2010 as Canada's first male saint
titleHook: Miracle Worker of St. Joseph's Oratory

name: St. Raymond of Penyafort
facts: Compiled the Decretals, the standard canon law collection used for centuries
Helped organize the Order of Preachers (Dominicans) with St. Dominic
Miraculously crossed the sea from Majorca to Barcelona on his cloak
Advised popes and kings while living as a Dominican friar
titleHook: Patron Saint of Canon Lawyers

name: St. Lawrence Giustiniani
facts: First Patriarch of Venice after the see was elevated in 1451
Renounced a noble marriage to join the Canons Regular of St. Augustine
Reformed clergy and promoted peace during Venice's golden age
Known for profound mystical writings on the Passion of Christ
titleHook: First Patriarch of Venice

name: St. Adrian of Canterbury
facts: African-born abbot who became Archbishop of Canterbury's chief advisor
Founded the school at Canterbury that trained generations of English clergy
Worked with St. Theodore of Tarsus to organize the English Church
His tomb at Canterbury was a pilgrimage site for centuries
titleHook: African Abbot Who Shaped English Christianity

name: St. William of Bourges
facts: Archbishop of Bourges who lived as a simple monk despite his rank
Participated in the Third Crusade and helped ransom Christian prisoners
Known for severe penances and nightly vigils in prayer
His incorrupt body was venerated until destroyed in the French Revolution
titleHook: Crusader Archbishop Who Lived Like a Monk

name: St. Theodosius the Cenobiarch
facts: Founded the first large cenobitic monastery in the Judean desert
Sheltered refugees during Samaritan revolts in Palestine
His Laura of St. Theodosius housed over 700 monks at its peak
Influenced St. Sabbas and the entire Eastern monastic tradition
titleHook: Father of Desert Monasticism in Palestine

name: St. Benedict Biscop
facts: Founded the twin monasteries of Wearmouth and Jarrow in England
Made five trips to Rome to bring books, art, and liturgical knowledge
His library at Jarrow educated the Venerable Bede
Introduced stone church architecture and glass windows to Anglo-Saxon England
titleHook: Monk Who Built England's Greatest Libraries

name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
facts: Called "Athanasius of the West" for defending Nicene orthodoxy
Wrote the first Latin commentary on the Gospel of Matthew
Exiled to Phrygia by Emperor Constantius II for four years
His writings on the Trinity influenced St. Augustine and St. Jerome
titleHook: Athanasius of the West

name: St. Felix of Nola
facts: Priest who hid from persecution in a ruined building where spiders wove a web over the entrance
Legend says he sold himself into slavery to free a Christian prisoner
Friend and supporter of St. Paulinus of Nola
Survived multiple attempts on his life during Decian persecution
titleHook: Priest Saved by a Spider's Web

name: St. Paul the First Hermit
facts: First Christian hermit; lived alone in the Egyptian desert for decades
Fed by a raven that brought him half a loaf of bread daily
Met St. Anthony the Great shortly before his death at age 113
Inspired the entire eremitical movement in Christianity
titleHook: First Christian Desert Hermit

name: St. Berard and Companions
facts: First Franciscan martyrs; killed preaching the Gospel in Morocco
St. Berard and four companions were stoned and beheaded at Ceuta
Their deaths inspired St. Anthony of Padua to join the Franciscans
Canonized by Pope Sixtus IV in 1481
titleHook: First Franciscan Martyrs in Morocco

name: St. Anthony of Egypt
facts: Father of monasticism; spent 20 years in complete solitude in the desert
Tempted by demons in visions recorded by St. Athanasius in his famous Life
His cloak became St. Athanasius's pallium; his staff held by St. Benedict
Still one of the most venerated saints in both East and West after 1,700 years
titleHook: Father of Christian Monasticism

name: St. Margaret of Hungary
facts: Royal princess who refused marriage to become a Dominican nun
Lived in extreme austerity and penance at the convent of Buda
Performed miracles of healing during her short life of 28 years
Canonized in 1943 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Princess Who Chose the Convent Over the Crown

name: St. Wulfstan
facts: Last surviving pre-Norman Conquest bishop in England
Persuaded William the Conqueror to abolish the slave trade at Bristol
Rebuilt Worcester Cathedral and lived in strict poverty
Known for healing miracles and tireless pastoral care
titleHook: Last Saxon Bishop of England

name: St. Sebastian
facts: Roman soldier who secretly converted fellow guards to Christianity
Survived being shot with arrows; later clubbed to death by order of Diocletian
One of the most depicted saints in Renaissance art
His martyrdom is commemorated in Rome's Church of San Sebastiano
titleHook: Martyr Who Survived the Emperor's Arrows

name: St. Agnes of Rome
facts: Martyred at age 12 or 13 for refusing to marry a Roman prefect
Name means lamb in Latin; lambs are blessed on her feast day at the Vatican
One of only seven women named in the Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I)
Her tomb in the Catacomb of St. Agnes is still visited today
titleHook: Child Martyr Whose Name Means Lamb

name: St. Vincent of Saragossa
facts: Deacon of Bishop Valerius; preached when the bishop could not speak
Tortured on a gridiron during Diocletian persecution in Saragossa
His relics were thrown into the sea but washed ashore and preserved
Patron of the Portuguese island of São Vicente in the Cape Verde archipelago
titleHook: Deacon Martyr of Saragossa

name: St. Marianne Cope
facts: Led Franciscan sisters to care for Hansen's disease patients in Hawaii
Worked alongside St. Damien of Molokai for five years before his death
Never contracted leprosy despite daily contact with patients for decades
Canonized in 2012 as one of the first American Franciscan saints
titleHook: Saint Who Served Hawaii's Leprosy Patients

name: St. Francis de Sales
facts: Bishop of Geneva who reconverted thousands through gentle persuasion
Wrote "Introduction to the Devout Life," a classic of spiritual direction
Co-founded the Order of the Visitation with St. Jane Frances de Chantal
Patron of writers and journalists since 1923
titleHook: Doctor of Gentle Spiritual Direction

name: St. Paul the Apostle
facts: Former persecutor Saul converted on the road to Damascus around AD 36
Feast of the Conversion of St. Paul commemorates his dramatic call to apostleship
Wrote 13 epistles that form a major part of the New Testament
Tradition holds he was beheaded in Rome under Nero around AD 67
titleHook: Apostle Converted on the Road to Damascus

name: St. Timothy and St. Titus
lifespan: Timothy: d. c. 97; Titus: d. c. 96
facts: Timothy was St. Paul's closest disciple and bishop of Ephesus
Titus organized the Church in Crete and was its first bishop
Both received personal letters from St. Paul preserved in the New Testament
Timothy's relics rest in the Cathedral of Termoli, Italy
titleHook: Paul's Trusted Disciples & Bishops

name: St. Angela Merici
facts: Founded the Ursulines, the first teaching order of women in the Church
Received a vision calling her to establish a company of virgins in Brescia
Worked tirelessly to educate poor girls in Renaissance Italy
Canonized in 1807; her order spread worldwide
titleHook: Founder of the First Teaching Order for Women

name: St. Thomas Aquinas
facts: Wrote the Summa Theologica, the masterwork of Catholic theology
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1567; patron of universities since 1880
Experienced a mystical vision that made all his writing seem like straw
His Eucharistic hymns Pange Lingua and Tantum Ergo are still sung today
titleHook: Angelic Doctor of the Catholic Church

name: St. Gildas the Wise
facts: Wrote De Excidio et Conquestu Britanniae, the earliest history of Britain
Monk who preached repentance to corrupt British kings
Associated with the legendary island monastery of Glastonbury
One of the few historical sources for post-Roman Britain
titleHook: Monk Who Wrote Britain's Earliest History

name: St. Hyacintha Mariscotti
facts: Noble woman who entered the Franciscan Third Order after a broken engagement
Transformed from vanity to radical charity at San Bernardino convent in Viterbo
Fed the poor, nursed the sick, and cared for prisoners for 40 years
Canonized in 1807 by Pope Pius VII
titleHook: Noble Woman Who Gave Everything to the Poor

name: St. John Bosco
facts: Founded the Salesians to educate poor and abandoned boys in Turin
Developed the Preventive System of education based on love, not punishment
Built oratories, schools, and missions on every continent
Canonized in 1934; his relics are venerated in Turin
titleHook: Apostle of Youth Who Founded the Salesians

name: St. Brigid of Ireland
facts: Founded the first monastery for women in Ireland at Kildare
Legend says her cloak expanded to claim land for her convent
Known for extraordinary charity to the poor and sick
One of Ireland's three patron saints alongside Patrick and Columba
titleHook: Patroness Who Founded Ireland's First Women's Abbey

name: Presentation of the Lord
facts: Mary and Joseph presented the infant Jesus in the Temple forty days after his birth
The prophet Simeon recognized Jesus as the light to the nations
Also called Candlemas; candles are blessed on this feast
Described in Luke 2:22–40 as a fulfillment of Mosaic law
titleHook: Feast of Light in the Temple

name: St. Blaise
facts: Bishop martyred under Licinius in the early fourth century
Legend says he saved a boy choking on a fish bone
Throats are blessed with crossed candles on his feast day
One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers venerated in medieval Europe
titleHook: Bishop Who Blesses Throats on His Feast

name: St. Joan of France
facts: Daughter of Louis XI who founded the Order of the Annunciation
Left an unhappy royal marriage to dedicate herself to God
Built hospitals and cared for the poor in Bourges
Canonized in 1950 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Princess Who Founded the Annunciation Order

name: St. Agatha of Sicily
facts: Martyred for refusing a Roman prefect during Decian persecution
Patroness of Catania; her intercession is credited with stopping Mount Etna eruptions
One of the most venerated virgin martyrs of the early Church
Her name appears in the Roman Canon of the Mass
titleHook: Virgin Martyr Patroness of Catania

name: St. Paul Miki and Companions
facts: Twenty-six Christians crucified at Nagasaki on February 5, 1597
Paul Miki, a Jesuit scholastic, preached from his cross until death
Included Franciscans, Jesuits, laymen, and three boys among the martyrs
Canonized in 1862 as the first Japanese martyrs
titleHook: Martyrs Crucified at Nagasaki

name: St. Colette of Corbie
facts: Reformed the Poor Clare order according to St. Francis's original rule
Established over seventeen convents across France and Savoy
Known for visions of the Passion and miracles of healing
The Colettine branch of Poor Clares still follows her strict observance
titleHook: Reformer of the Poor Clare Order

name: St. Josephine Bakhita
facts: Kidnapped and enslaved as a child in Sudan before gaining freedom in Italy
Became a Canossian sister known for her joyful spirit and forgiveness
First Sudanese saint; canonized in 2000 by Pope John Paul II
Her name Bakhita means fortunate in Arabic
titleHook: From Slavery to Sainthood in Italy

name: St. Apollonia
facts: Deaconess martyred during persecution under Emperor Decius
Had all her teeth broken or pulled out before being burned alive
Patroness of dentists since the Middle Ages
One of the early Church's most venerated Alexandrian martyrs
titleHook: Patroness of Dentists and Toothache

name: St. Scholastica
facts: Twin sister of St. Benedict; founded a convent at Plombariola
Their final meeting ended with a miraculous storm prolonging their conversation
Died three days after that meeting; Benedict saw her soul ascend as a dove
Patroness of Benedictine nuns worldwide
titleHook: Twin Sister of St. Benedict

name: Our Lady of Lourdes
facts: The Blessed Virgin appeared to St. Bernadette Soubirous eighteen times in 1858
Identified herself as the Immaculate Conception at the grotto of Massabielle
Lourdes has become one of the world's greatest pilgrimage sites for healing
Millions of pilgrims visit the spring Bernadette uncovered each year
titleHook: Immaculate Conception Appears at Lourdes

name: St. Eulalia of Barcelona
facts: Thirteen-year-old martyr who endured thirteen tortures before death
Patroness of Barcelona; her martyrdom is depicted in the cathedral
Legend says a dove flew from her mouth at death carrying her soul to heaven
One of the most celebrated virgin martyrs of Roman Spain
titleHook: Child Martyr Patroness of Barcelona

name: St. Catherine de' Ricci
facts: Dominican mystic who experienced weekly ecstasies of the Passion for twelve years
Bilocation miracles were reported during her ecstasies
Served as prioress of San Vincenzo convent in Prato for thirty-six years
Canonized in 1746; known for wise spiritual counsel to bishops and princes
titleHook: Mystic Who Relived the Passion Weekly

name: Sts. Cyril and Methodius
facts: Created the Glagolitic alphabet to translate Scripture into Slavonic
Apostles to the Slavs; evangelized Moravia and Pannonia
Their liturgy in the vernacular shaped Eastern European Christianity
Named co-patrons of Europe by Pope John Paul II in 1980
titleHook: Apostles to the Slavs and Europe's Patrons

name: St. Claude la Colombière
facts: Spiritual director of St. Margaret Mary Alacoque who spread devotion to the Sacred Heart
Confessor to the English court at St. James Palace in London
Imprisoned and exiled for alleged involvement in the Popish Plot
Beatified for his role in promoting the Sacred Heart revelations
titleHook: Apostle of the Sacred Heart Devotion

name: St. Juliana of Nicomedia
facts: Martyred for refusing to marry a pagan Roman senator
Endured boiling in oil and other tortures before beheading
Her cult spread widely in both East and West from the fourth century
Patroness of sick people in many medieval hospitals
titleHook: Martyr Who Refused a Pagan Marriage

name: Seven Holy Founders of the Servites
facts: Seven wealthy Florentine merchants who withdrew to serve Our Lady of Sorrows
Founded the Order of Servites in 1233 on Monte Senario
Received a vision of the Blessed Virgin encouraging their community
Canonized together in 1888 by Pope Leo XIII
titleHook: Merchants Who Founded the Servite Order

name: St. Bernadette Soubirous
facts: Received eighteen apparitions of the Blessed Virgin at Lourdes in 1858
Lived as a humble nun at Nevers despite worldwide fame
Her incorrupt body is venerated at the convent of Saint-Gildard
Canonized in 1933; never returned to Lourdes after leaving as a novice
titleHook: Visionary of the Lourdes Apparitions

name: St. Conrad of Piacenza
facts: Nobleman who became a hermit after accidentally causing a forest fire
Lived forty years in a cave near Noto in Sicily
Known for miracles of healing and prophecy among local villagers
Canonized in 1625 for his extraordinary penitential life
titleHook: Hermit Who Lived Forty Years in a Cave

name: St. Wulfric of Haselbury
facts: Parish priest who lived as a hermit attached to his church for twenty-nine years
Wore a hair shirt and chain; ate only barley bread and vegetables
Known for prophecy and healing miracles throughout Somerset
His cell became a pilgrimage site after his death
titleHook: Hermit Priest of Haselbury Plucknett

name: St. Peter Damian
facts: Cardinal and Doctor of the Church who reformed clerical life
Wrote against simony and clerical corruption in the eleventh century
Advisor to Pope Gregory VII during the Investiture Controversy
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1828 by Pope Leo XII
titleHook: Doctor Who Reformed the Medieval Church

name: Chair of St. Peter
facts: Celebrates the authority of the papal office established by Christ on Peter
Commemorates Peter's founding of the Church in Rome
The relic of Peter's chair is venerated at St. Peter's Basilica
Ancient feast dating to at least the fourth century in Rome
titleHook: Feast of the Papal Authority of Peter

name: St. Polycarp of Smyrna
facts: Disciple of St. John the Apostle and bishop of Smyrna
One of the Apostolic Fathers; his martyrdom account is among the earliest
Burned at the stake; the flames formed an arch around his body
Refused to revile Christ before the Roman proconsul at age eighty-six
titleHook: Apostolic Father Burned at the Stake

name: St. Matthias the Apostle
facts: Chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve Apostles
Preached the Gospel in Judea and according to tradition in Ethiopia
His election is recorded in Acts 1:15–26
Tradition holds he was martyred by stoning and beheading
titleHook: Apostle Chosen to Replace Judas

name: St. Walburga
facts: English missionary nun who helped evangelize Germany with St. Boniface
Abbess of Heidenheim; her relics exude a healing oil called Walburga's oil
Her brother St. Willibald was the first Englishman to write a travelogue
Patroness of Bavaria and one of Germany's most beloved saints
titleHook: Abbess Whose Relics Exude Healing Oil

name: St. Porphyry of Gaza
facts: Bishop of Gaza who destroyed pagan temples and built churches
Sold his inheritance to ransom captives and aid the poor
Known for miracles that converted many pagans in Gaza
His life was written by his deacon Mark the Deacon
titleHook: Bishop Who Converted Pagan Gaza

name: St. Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows
facts: Passionist clerical student who died at age twenty-four of tuberculosis
Known for extraordinary devotion to the Sorrowful Mother
His life inspired countless young people to holiness
Canonized in 1920 by Pope Benedict XV
titleHook: Young Passionist Devoted to Our Lady of Sorrows

name: St. Romaric
facts: Frankish nobleman who founded the double monastery of Remiremont
Converted by St. Amatus after the death of his wife
Sheltered refugees and established one of the great abbeys of Lorraine
His monastery became a center of learning and charity
titleHook: Nobleman Who Founded Remiremont Abbey

name: St. David of Wales
facts: Patron saint of Wales; founded twelve monasteries across South Wales
Known for austere monastic rule and teaching monks to plow fields themselves
His last words urged followers to do the little things faithfully
His shrine at St. David's Cathedral was a major medieval pilgrimage
titleHook: Patron Saint of Wales

name: St. Agnes of Prague
facts: Bohemian princess who became a Poor Clare nun despite royal opposition
Built a hospital for the poor and cared for lepers personally
Corresponded with St. Clare of Assisi and lived her rule strictly
Known for miracles during her life and after her death
titleHook: Princess Who Became a Poor Clare Nun

name: St. Katharine Drexel
facts: Heiress who gave away her fortune to found schools for Native and African Americans
Established Xavier University in New Orleans, the first Black Catholic college
Founded the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament in 1891
Second American-born saint; canonized in 2000
titleHook: Heiress Who Built Schools for the Marginalized

name: St. Casimir
facts: Polish-Lithuanian prince known for chastity, prayer, and charity to the poor
Refused marriage and devoted himself to prayer and service
Patron saint of Lithuania and Poland
Died of tuberculosis at age twenty-five; canonized in 1522
titleHook: Prince Who Chose Prayer Over Power

name: St. John Joseph of the Cross
facts: Franciscan priest known for extreme austerity and gift of reading souls
Served as novice master and provincial of the Alcantarine Franciscans
Performed numerous miracles of healing and bilocation
Canonized in 1839 by Pope Gregory XVI
titleHook: Franciscan Mystic of Calabria

name: St. Chrodegang of Metz
facts: Bishop of Metz who reformed clergy life through the Rule of Chrodegang
Advisor to Pepin the Short and Charlemagne's grandfather
Introduced communal life for cathedral canons in the Frankish Church
His rule influenced medieval cathedral chapters across Europe
titleHook: Bishop Who Reformed Frankish Cathedral Clergy

name: Sts. Perpetua and Felicity
facts: Perpetua kept a prison diary, one of the earliest Christian texts by a woman
Felicity gave birth in prison hours before both were sent to the arena
Martyred in Carthage during persecution under Septimius Severus
Their Passion account is read annually in the Liturgy of the Hours
titleHook: Martyrs of Carthage Whose Diary Survives

name: St. John of God
facts: Founded the Brothers Hospitallers to care for the sick and poor
Experienced a dramatic conversion after hearing a sermon by St. John of Avila
Carried the sick on his back and sold everything to fund his hospital
Patron of hospitals and the sick; canonized in 1690
titleHook: Founder Who Carried the Sick on His Back

name: St. Frances of Rome
facts: Founded the Oblates of Tor de' Specchi for widowed women in Rome
Experienced visions of her guardian angel throughout her married life
Organized relief for the poor during plague and civil war in Rome
Canonized in 1608; her order still serves in Rome today
titleHook: Widow Who Founded the Oblates of Rome

name: St. John Ogilvie
facts: Jesuit priest martyred in Glasgow for celebrating Mass during persecution
Only post-Reformation Scottish saint canonized by the Catholic Church
Hanged and drawn at Glasgow Cross on March 10, 1615
Canonized in 1976 by Pope Paul VI
titleHook: Scotland's Post-Reformation Martyr

name: St. Constantine
facts: Cornish king who abdicated his throne to become a monk
Associated with the evangelization of Scotland and Cornwall
Legend connects him to the missionary work of St. Columba
Represents royal conversion to monastic life in Celtic Christianity
titleHook: King Who Abdicated to Become a Monk

name: St. Maximilian of Tebessa
facts: Roman soldier executed for refusing military service as a Christian
One of the earliest recorded conscientious objectors in Christian history
His trial record survives as an important early Christian document
Venerated as a martyr for refusing to bear arms
titleHook: Soldier Martyr Who Refused to Fight

name: St. Leander of Seville
facts: Archbishop of Seville who converted the Visigoths from Arianism
Brother of St. Isidore of Seville and St. Fulgentius of Cartagena
Presided over councils that established Catholic orthodoxy in Spain
Mentor of St. Gregory the Great during his time in Constantinople
titleHook: Archbishop Who Converted Visigothic Spain

name: St. Matilda of Saxony
facts: Queen of Germany and wife of King Henry the Fowler
Founded monasteries and hospitals throughout Saxony
Known for extraordinary charity and reconciliation of feuding nobles
Patroness invoked by mothers with difficult children
titleHook: Queen Who Built Monasteries Across Saxony

name: St. Longinus
facts: Roman centurion who pierced Christ's side with a spear at the Crucifixion
Tradition says blood and water from the wound healed his failing eyesight
Converted immediately and later martyred for his faith
The Holy Lance relic is venerated in several churches
titleHook: Centurion Who Pierced Christ's Side

name: St. Abban of Magheranoidhe
facts: Irish abbot and missionary associated with St. Kevin of Glendalough
Founded monasteries and churches along Ireland's eastern coast
Legends tell of miraculous escapes from pagan persecutors
Part of the great wave of Irish monastic founders
titleHook: Irish Abbot and Missionary

name: St. Patrick
facts: Kidnapped to Ireland as a slave; returned as a missionary bishop
Used the shamrock to explain the Holy Trinity to the Irish
Established monasteries and churches throughout Ireland
Patron saint of Ireland; feast celebrated worldwide
titleHook: Apostle and Patron Saint of Ireland

name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
facts: Patriarch of Jerusalem and Doctor of the Church
His Catechetical Lectures remain a foundation of Christian instruction
Defended orthodoxy against Arianism at the Council of Constantinople
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1883 by Pope Leo XIII
titleHook: Doctor Who Taught the Catechumens of Jerusalem

name: St. Joseph
facts: Foster father of Jesus and husband of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Patron of the Universal Church declared by Pope Pius IX in 1870
Named patron of workers by Pope Pius XII in 1955
His feast on March 19 has been celebrated since the tenth century
titleHook: Patron of the Universal Church and Workers

name: St. Cuthbert of Lindisfarne
facts: Bishop of Lindisfarne and one of England's most beloved saints
Known for healing miracles and gift of prophecy
Hermit on Inner Farne island before becoming bishop
His body was found incorrupt when his tomb was opened
titleHook: Bishop-Hermit of Holy Lindisfarne

name: St. Nicholas of Flüe
facts: Swiss hermit and peacemaker who prevented civil war in the Swiss Confederation
Left his family to live as a hermit after a vision at age fifty
His counsel was sought by Swiss cantons during political crises
Patron saint of Switzerland; canonized in 1947
titleHook: Hermit Who Prevented Swiss Civil War

name: St. Lea of Rome
facts: Wealthy Roman widow who entered a convent after her husband's death
Her funeral was attended by St. Jerome who wrote a moving eulogy
Renounced luxury to live in poverty and prayer
Jerome praised her as a model for consecrated widows
titleHook: Widow Praised by St. Jerome

name: St. Turibius of Mogrovejo
facts: Archbishop of Lima who traveled 25,000 miles visiting his vast diocese
Fought for the rights of indigenous peoples against Spanish colonists
Confirmed St. Rose of Lima, Martin de Porres, and Juan Macias
Canonized in 1726 as a model missionary bishop
titleHook: Bishop Who Defended Indigenous Peoples

name: St. Catherine of Sweden
facts: Daughter of St. Bridget of Sweden; abbess of Vadstena Abbey
Made pilgrimages to Rome and the Holy Land with her mother
Lived in strict observance of the Bridgettine rule
Known for visions and deep devotion to the Passion
titleHook: Bridgettine Abbess and Pilgrim

name: Annunciation of the Lord
facts: The angel Gabriel announced to Mary that she would conceive the Son of God
Mary's fiat — Let it be done — marks the moment of the Incarnation
Nine months before Christmas; also called Lady Day
Described in Luke 1:26–38; a pivotal moment in salvation history
titleHook: Feast of the Incarnation at Nazareth

name: St. Braulio of Zaragoza
facts: Bishop of Zaragoza and advisor to Visigothic kings
Completed St. Isidore of Seville's Etymologies after his death
Wrote a life of St. Emilian and promoted monasticism in Spain
One of the great scholars of Visigothic Spain
titleHook: Bishop-Scholar of Visigothic Spain

name: St. John of Egypt
facts: Desert hermit who lived in a cave for fifty years
Received visitors including Emperor Theodosius seeking spiritual counsel
Known for gift of prophecy and reading hearts
His life inspired generations of Egyptian desert monks
titleHook: Desert Hermit Who Advised Emperors

name: St. Gontran
facts: Frankish king who repented of a violent life and lived in penance
Protected the Church and founded monasteries in Burgundy
Known for justice and charity after his conversion
Patron of repentant sinners in medieval France
titleHook: King Who Repented and Lived in Penance

name: St. Berthold of Calabria
facts: Traditionally considered founder of the Carmelite order on Mount Carmel
Led hermits who settled near the prophet Elijah's cave
Established the rule that shaped Carmelite spirituality
His feast connects Carmelites to their Mount Carmel origins
titleHook: Founder of the Carmelite Hermits

name: St. John Climacus
facts: Monk of Mount Sinai who wrote The Ladder of Divine Ascent
Abbot of Mount Sinai monastery for his final years
His Ladder describes thirty steps of spiritual progress
One of the most influential spiritual writers of Eastern Christianity
titleHook: Author of The Ladder of Divine Ascent

name: St. Stephen of Mar Saba
facts: Monk of the Great Lavra of Mar Saba for over fifty years
Lived the last years of his life in complete solitude in a cell
Known for visions and miracles reported by pilgrims
Represented the pinnacle of Palestinian desert monasticism
titleHook: Monk of the Great Lavra of Mar Saba

name: St. Hugh of Grenoble
facts: Bishop of Grenoble who supported St. Bruno in founding the Carthusians
Reformed his diocese and retired to a Carthusian monastery twice
Known for healing miracles and defense of Church rights
His reform of Grenoble lasted over fifty years
titleHook: Bishop Who Helped Found the Carthusians

name: St. Francis of Paola
facts: Founded the Minim Friars, known for the vow of perpetual Lent
Performed miracles including walking on water and raising the dead
Called to France by Louis XI and served as counselor to French kings
Patron of Calabria; canonized in 1519
titleHook: Founder of the Minim Friars

name: St. Richard of Chichester
facts: Bishop of Chichester who rebuilt his cathedral after royal opposition
Known for poverty, preaching, and care for the sick
His famous prayer — Day by day, dear Lord — is widely used today
Canonized in 1262; shrine at Chichester Cathedral until the Reformation
titleHook: Bishop Whose Prayer Is Still Recited Today

name: St. Isidore of Seville
facts: Archbishop of Seville and last Father of the Western Church
His Etymologies encyclopedia preserved classical knowledge for centuries
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1722; patron of the internet since 1997
Presided over councils that shaped Spanish Catholic identity
titleHook: Doctor of the Church and Patron of the Internet

name: St. Vincent Ferrer
facts: Dominican preacher who traveled across Europe calling for repentance
Said to have converted thousands through his apocalyptic preaching
Performed miracles including raising the dead and healing the blind
Patron of builders and orphanages in Valencia
titleHook: Dominican Preacher of the Apocalypse

name: St. William of Eskilsoe
facts: English-born abbot who reformed monastic life in Denmark
Introduced strict Benedictine observance at Eskilsoe Abbey
Known for miracles and gift of prophecy
Helped establish monasticism in medieval Scandinavia
titleHook: Abbot Who Brought Benedictine Reform to Denmark

name: St. John Baptist de La Salle
facts: Founder of the Brothers of the Christian Schools
Pioneered free education for the poor and training of lay teachers
Declared patron of all teachers of youth in 1950
Canonized in 1900; first institute for lay brothers in the Church
titleHook: Founder of Christian Schools for the Poor

name: St. Julie Billiart
facts: Founded the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur during the French Revolution
Paralyzed for twenty-two years before being miraculously healed
Established schools for poor girls across France and Belgium
Canonized in 1969 by Pope Paul VI
titleHook: Founder Who Was Healed After Twenty-Two Years

name: St. Casilda of Toledo
facts: Muslim princess who converted to Christianity after a miraculous healing
Lived as a hermit near the Tagus River caring for the poor
Her tomb in Burgos became a pilgrimage site
Patroness of Toledo and symbol of religious reconciliation
titleHook: Princess Convert Who Became a Hermit

name: St. Michael de Sanctis
facts: Trinitarian friar who died at age thirty-three after a life of extreme penance
Known for ecstatic visions during Mass and deep Trinitarian devotion
Served as master of novices and preacher despite his youth
Canonized in 1862 as a model of Trinitarian spirituality
titleHook: Young Trinitarian Mystic of Catalonia

name: St. Stanislaus of Kraków
facts: Bishop of Kraków martyred by King Bolesław II for denouncing injustice
His murder triggered a rebellion that deposed the king
One of Poland's primary patron saints alongside St. Wojciech
Canonized in 1253; his feast is a major celebration in Poland
titleHook: Bishop Martyr and Patron of Poland

name: St. Teresa of the Andes
facts: First Chilean and first Discalced Carmelite from the Americas to be canonized
Entered Carmel at age nineteen and died of typhus at twenty
Her spiritual diary reveals extraordinary maturity and joy
Canonized in 1993 by Pope John Paul II
titleHook: First Carmelite Saint of the Americas

name: St. Martin I
facts: Pope who condemned Monothelitism at the Lateran Council of 649
Arrested by Emperor Constans II and exiled to Crimea
Died of starvation and mistreatment in exile
Last pope venerated as a martyr in the Church
titleHook: Pope Martyr Who Defended Orthodoxy

name: St. Benedict Joseph Labre
facts: Homeless pilgrim who visited every major shrine in Europe on foot
Lived entirely on alms and slept outdoors or in ruins
Known for ecstatic prayer and deep devotion to the Eucharist
Died on the steps of a Roman church; canonized in 1881
titleHook: Homeless Pilgrim of the European Shrines

name: St. Ruadhan of Lorrha
facts: Irish abbot who founded the monastery of Lorrha in Tipperary
Associated with the curse of Tara in Irish ecclesiastical legend
Contemporary of St. Brendan and St. Columba
One of the twelve apostles of Ireland in tradition
titleHook: Irish Abbot of Lorrha Monastery

name: St. Drogo of Sebourg
facts: Shepherd who became a pilgrim and hermit after a disfiguring illness
Lived in a cell attached to a church for forty years
Known for bilocation miracles reported by multiple witnesses
Patron of those whom others find repulsive or unwell
titleHook: Hermit Who Was Seen in Two Places at Once

name: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
facts: First Native American saint; Mohawk-Algonquin convert
Known as the Lily of the Mohawks for her purity and devotion
Endured persecution from her tribe for her Catholic faith
Canonized in 2012 by Pope Benedict XVI
titleHook: Lily of the Mohawks — First Native American Saint

name: St. Apollonius the Apologist
facts: Christian philosopher whose Apology defended the faith before the Senate
Martyred under Commodus for refusing to renounce Christianity
His defense argued Christians were loyal citizens and moral people
One of the earliest Christian apologetic texts to survive
titleHook: Philosopher Martyr Who Defended Christianity

name: St. Expeditus
facts: Roman soldier martyr venerated for intercession in urgent matters
Popular devotion spread from Sicily and France in the nineteenth century
Invoked against procrastination and for swift resolution of problems
His cult reflects the Church's pastoral response to popular piety
titleHook: Martyr Invoked for Urgent Causes

name: St. Agnes of Montepulciano
facts: Dominican abbess who founded a convent in Montepulciano at age fifteen
St. Catherine of Siena knelt in devotion at her incorrupt body
Known for miracles including multiplying bread and raising the dead
Canonized in 1726 by Pope Benedict XIII
titleHook: Dominican Abbess Whom Catherine of Siena Venerated

name: St. Anselm of Canterbury
facts: Archbishop of Canterbury and father of Scholastic theology
His Proslogion contains the famous ontological argument for God
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1720
Balanced contemplative prayer with rigorous intellectual inquiry
titleHook: Father of Scholastic Theology

name: St. Soter and St. Caius
facts: Early popes who strengthened the Church during Roman persecution
St. Soter is credited with instituting the marriage sacrament blessing
Both buried in the catacombs of Callixtus in Rome
Their tombs were venerated by early Christian pilgrims
titleHook: Early Popes of the Roman Church

name: St. George
facts: Roman soldier martyred under Diocletian for refusing to renounce Christ
Legend of slaying a dragon symbolizes victory over evil
Patron saint of England and many other nations and regions
One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers of medieval devotion
titleHook: Dragon-Slaying Martyr and Patron of England

name: St. Fidelis of Sigmaringen
facts: Capuchin friar martyred while preaching to Swiss Calvinists
Former lawyer who gave up wealth to join the Capuchins
First martyr of the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith
Canonized in 1746 by Pope Benedict XIV
titleHook: Capuchin Martyr of the Counter-Reformation

name: St. Mark the Evangelist
facts: Author of the second Gospel and companion of St. Peter
Tradition holds he founded the Church in Alexandria, Egypt
Patron saint of Venice; his symbol is the winged lion
His relics were smuggled from Alexandria to Venice in 828
titleHook: Evangelist and Patron of Venice

name: Our Lady of Good Counsel
facts: Miraculous image of the Madonna appeared in Genazzano on April 25, 1467
The fresco is venerated for granting counsel and healing
Pope Leo XIII added the title to the Litany of Loreto in 1903
Shrine in Genazzano draws pilgrims from around the world
titleHook: Madonna of Good Counsel at Genazzano

name: St. Zita of Lucca
facts: Domestic servant known for charity and miracles over forty-eight years
Shared food with the poor and cared for sick prisoners
Her body is incorrupt in the Basilica of San Frediano, Lucca
Patroness of domestic workers since 1696
titleHook: Servant Saint of Lucca

name: St. Peter Chanel
facts: First martyr of Oceania; Marist missionary to Futuna island
Killed by the king's son for converting his son to Christianity
Entire island converted within months of his martyrdom
Canonized in 1954 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: First Martyr of Oceania

name: St. Catherine of Siena
facts: Dominican mystic who persuaded Pope Gregory XI to return to Rome
Doctor of the Church; one of the first two women so declared
Her Dialogue is a masterpiece of mystical theology
Patroness of Italy and Europe alongside St. Francis of Assisi
titleHook: Doctor Who Brought the Pope Back to Rome

name: St. Pius V
facts: Pope who implemented the Council of Trent reforms
Organized the Holy League victory at Lepanto in 1571
Standardized the Roman Missal used until Vatican II
Canonized in 1712 for his reforming papacy
titleHook: Pope Who Standardized the Roman Missal

name: St. Joseph the Worker
facts: Feast instituted by Pope Pius XII in 1955 to honor dignified labor
Joseph taught Jesus the trade of carpentry in Nazareth
Patron of workers alongside his March 19 solemnity
Counterbalances secular May Day with a Catholic vision of work
titleHook: Patron of Workers on May Day

name: St. Athanasius of Alexandria
facts: Champion of Nicene orthodoxy against Arianism throughout his life
Bishop of Alexandria for forty-five years despite five exiles
Wrote the Life of St. Anthony that spread monasticism to the West
Called Athanasius Contra Mundum — Athanasius against the world
titleHook: Champion of Nicene Orthodoxy

name: Sts. Philip and James the Apostles
facts: Philip brought Nathanael to Jesus; asked to see the Father at the Last Supper
James the Less authored the New Testament epistle of James
Both apostles preached and were martyred for the faith
Their relics are honored at the Church of the Twelve Apostles in Rome
titleHook: Apostles Who Preached Christ to the Nations

name: St. Florian of Lorch
facts: Roman officer martyred for refusing to persecute Christians
Thrown into the Enns River with a millstone around his neck
Patron saint of firefighters and Austria
His intercession is invoked against fire and flood
titleHook: Patron Saint of Firefighters

name: St. Hilary of Arles
facts: Archbishop of Arles who led the Church in Gaul
Disciple of St. Honoratus of Lérins
Known for monastic reform and theological writings
His see was one of the most important in early medieval Gaul
titleHook: Archbishop Who Led the Church in Gaul

name: St. Dominic Savio
facts: Student of St. John Bosco who died at age fourteen
Known for extraordinary piety and devotion to the Eucharist
Organized the Immaculate Conception Sodality among his peers
Youngest non-martyr saint in the Church; canonized in 1954
titleHook: Youngest Non-Martyr Saint in the Church

name: St. Rose Venerini
facts: Founded the Venerini Sisters to educate girls in central Italy
Opened free schools for poor girls in Viterbo and Rome
Her congregation spread education across Italy and to the United States
Canonized in 2006 by Pope Benedict XVI
titleHook: Founder Who Educated Poor Girls in Italy

name: St. Peter of Tarsus
facts: Monk and bishop who defended icons during the Iconoclast controversy
Imprisoned and tortured for refusing to destroy sacred images
His steadfastness helped preserve icon veneration in the East
Represented the martyrs of the Iconoclast persecution
titleHook: Defender of Sacred Icons in Byzantium

name: St. Pachomius the Great
facts: Founder of cenobitic (communal) monasticism in Christianity
Organized thousands of monks into structured communities with rules
Former soldier who converted after Christians aided him in prison
His rule influenced St. Basil and all Western monasticism
titleHook: Founder of Communal Monasticism

name: St. Damien of Molokai
facts: Belgian priest who served Hansen's disease patients on Molokai
Built churches, schools, and homes before contracting leprosy himself
Continued serving his flock until his death at age forty-nine
Canonized in 2009 by Pope Benedict XVI
titleHook: Priest Who Served Hawaii's Leprosy Colony

name: St. Ignatius of Laconi
facts: Capuchin lay brother who begged alms for his friary for forty years
Known for miracles of healing and prophecy among the Sardinian poor
His crutches are venerated as relics in Cagliari
Canonized in 1951 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Capuchin Beggar-Brother of Sardinia

name: St. Nereus and St. Achilleus
facts: Roman soldiers converted to Christianity and martyred under Diocletian
Their ancient basilica in Rome was rebuilt by Pope St. Damasus
Damasus wrote their epitaph praising their faith and courage
Among the earliest martyrs venerated in the Roman catacombs
titleHook: Soldier Martyrs of the Roman Catacombs

name: Our Lady of Fatima
facts: The Blessed Virgin appeared to three shepherd children six times in 1917
Delivered messages of prayer, penance, and consecration of Russia
Miracle of the Sun witnessed by 70,000 on October 13, 1917
One of the most visited Marian shrines in the world today
titleHook: Our Lady Who Appeared to Three Shepherd Children

name: St. Carthage of Lismore
facts: Irish abbot who founded the monastery of Lismore in County Waterford
His monastery became one of the great centers of Irish learning
Previously abbot of Rahan with over eight hundred monks
Known for miracles and strict monastic discipline
titleHook: Abbot Who Founded Lismore Monastery

name: St. Isidore the Farmer
facts: Husband and farm laborer known for attending Mass before work daily
Angels were said to plow his fields while he prayed in church
Patron of farmers and rural communities in Spain and the Americas
Canonized in 1622 alongside St. Ignatius and St. Teresa
titleHook: Farmer Whose Angels Plowed His Fields

name: St. Brendan the Navigator
facts: Irish abbot who legend says sailed across the Atlantic in a currach
Founded monasteries including Clonfert in County Galway
The Navigatio Sancti Brendani inspired medieval exploration
Patron of sailors and one of Ireland's twelve apostles
titleHook: Abbot Who Legend Says Reached America

name: St. Paschal Baylon
facts: Franciscan lay brother with extraordinary devotion to the Eucharist
Known for ecstatic visions during Mass and Eucharistic adoration
Patron of Eucharistic congresses and associations
Canonized in 1690 for his profound sacramental piety
titleHook: Patron of Eucharistic Congresses

name: St. John I
facts: Pope sent by Theodoric the Ostrogoth to negotiate in Constantinople
Imprisoned and starved to death upon his return to Ravenna
Last pope to be venerated as a martyr for many centuries
His death marked growing tension between Rome and Arian rulers
titleHook: Pope Martyr of Ravenna

name: St. Celestine V
facts: Hermit pope who resigned after five months as Pope Celestine V in 1294
Founded the Celestine order of Benedictine monks
Dante placed him in Inferno for his great refusal
Canonized in 1313; his resignation legitimized papal abdication
titleHook: Hermit Pope Who Chose to Resign

name: St. Bernardino of Siena
facts: Franciscan preacher who popularized devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus
Traveled across Italy preaching repentance and charity
The IHS monogram he promoted appears in churches worldwide
Patron of advertisers for his innovative use of visual symbols
titleHook: Franciscan Preacher of the Holy Name

name: St. Christopher Magallanes
facts: Mexican priest martyred during the Cristero War for celebrating Mass
Built schools and catechized indigenous communities in Jalisco
Shot without trial on May 21, 1927 alongside companions
Canonized in 2000 as one of the Mexican martyrs
titleHook: Mexican Priest Martyr of the Cristero War

name: St. Rita of Cascia
facts: Augustinian nun known as the Saint of the Impossible
Bore a stigmata wound on her forehead resembling a thorn
Endured an abusive marriage and the murder of her sons
Canonized in 1900; one of the most popular saints of Italy
titleHook: Saint of the Impossible

name: St. John Baptist Rossi
facts: Roman priest who spent forty years serving prisoners and the poor
Known for gift of reading souls and miraculous conversions
Refused ecclesiastical honors to remain a simple parish priest
Canonized in 1881 for his tireless pastoral charity
titleHook: Priest Who Served Rome's Forgotten Poor

name: St. Vincent of Lérins
facts: Monk whose Commonitorium defined Catholic tradition as universal, ancient, and consensus
His formula remains a cornerstone of Catholic theological method
Contemporary of St. Patrick who studied at Lérins
One of the most quoted patristic authors on tradition
titleHook: Monk Who Defined Catholic Tradition

name: St. Bede the Venerable
facts: Monk of Jarrow and father of English history
Wrote the Ecclesiastical History of the English People
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1899 as the only English Doctor
His biblical commentaries shaped medieval exegesis
titleHook: Father of English History and Doctor of the Church

name: St. Philip Neri
facts: Founded the Oratory and renewed Rome through joy and prayer
Known for holy humor and making church attendance appealing to youth
Experienced ecstasies during Mass that lifted him off the ground
Called the Apostle of Rome; canonized in 1622
titleHook: Apostle of Rome and Saint of Holy Joy

name: St. Augustine of Canterbury
facts: Benedictine monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great to evangelize England
First Archbishop of Canterbury and apostle to the Anglo-Saxons
Baptized King Ethelbert of Kent, opening England to Christianity
His mission shaped the entire English Church for centuries
titleHook: Apostle Who Brought Christianity to England

name: St. Germanus of Paris
facts: Bishop of Paris who defended the Church against barbarian invasions
Rebuilt churches and cared for the poor during Frankish wars
His shrine at Saint-Germain-des-Prés was a major Paris pilgrimage
Patron of the disabled and protector of Paris
titleHook: Bishop Who Defended Paris from Invaders

name: St. Maximinus of Trier
facts: Bishop of Trier who hosted the Council of Trier in 326
Contemporary and ally of St. Athanasius against Arianism
His see was one of the oldest and most important in Germany
Built the first great basilica at Trier
titleHook: Bishop of One of Germany's Oldest Sees

name: St. Joan of Arc
facts: Teenage visionary who led French armies to victory during the Hundred Years War
Burned at the stake at age nineteen for heresy and witchcraft
Rehabilitated in 1456; canonized in 1920 by Pope Benedict XV
Patroness of France and one of history's most celebrated saints
titleHook: Warrior Maiden and Patroness of France

name: Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
facts: Mary visited her cousin Elizabeth who was pregnant with John the Baptist
Elizabeth's greeting — Blessed are you among women — begins the Hail Mary
Mary's Magnificat is one of the Church's greatest hymns of praise
Instituted by St. Francis de Sales and St. Jane Frances de Chantal
titleHook: Feast of Mary Visiting Elizabeth

name: St. Justin Martyr
facts: Christian philosopher who converted after studying Plato and Stoicism
Wrote two Apologies defending Christianity to Emperor Antoninus Pius
First Christian writer to describe the Eucharistic liturgy in detail
Beheaded in Rome for refusing to sacrifice to Roman gods
titleHook: Philosopher Martyr Who Described the Mass

name: Sts. Marcellinus and Peter
facts: Priest and exorcist martyred during Diocletian persecution in Rome
Buried in the catacomb that bears their names on the Via Labicana
Pope St. Damasus wrote inscriptions honoring their sacrifice
Their basilica was a major pilgrimage site in early Christian Rome
titleHook: Priest and Exorcist Martyrs of Rome

name: St. Charles Lwanga and Companions
facts: Twenty-two Ugandan martyrs burned alive by King Mwanga II
Charles Lwanga protected young pages from the king's immoral demands
First African martyrs canonized; feast celebrated across the continent
Canonized in 1964 by Pope Paul VI as witnesses to chastity and faith
titleHook: Ugandan Martyrs Who Died for Chastity

name: St. Optatus of Milevis
facts: Bishop who wrote against Donatism defending the unity of the Church
His six books against Parmenian shaped Catholic ecclesiology
Contemporary of St. Augustine in the North African Church
Defended the validity of sacraments administered by unworthy ministers
titleHook: Bishop Who Defended Church Unity Against Donatism

name: St. Boniface of Mainz
facts: English monk who evangelized Germany and became Archbishop of Mainz
Chopped down the sacred oak of Thor at Geismar to prove Christ's power
Martyred with fifty-two companions in Frisia at age seventy-nine
Apostle of Germany; reorganized the Frankish Church
titleHook: Apostle of Germany Martyred in Frisia

name: St. Norbert of Xanten
facts: Founder of the Premonstratensian order of canons regular
Archbishop of Magdeburg who reformed clergy and fought heresy
Known for preaching peace during the Investiture Controversy
His order combined monastic life with active pastoral ministry
titleHook: Founder of the Premonstratensian Order

name: St. Robert of Newminster
facts: Cistercian abbot who founded Newminster Abbey in Northumberland
Disciple of St. Bernard of Clairvaux at Rievaulx Abbey
Known for miracles of healing and multiplying food for his monks
His abbey became a center of Cistercian spirituality in England
titleHook: Cistercian Abbot of Newminster

name: St. Medard of Noyon
facts: Bishop of Noyon and Tournai who evangelized the Franks
Legend says laughter on his feast predicts forty days of rain or sun
Known for charity to the poor and rebuilding churches after wars
One of the most popular saints in medieval France
titleHook: Bishop Whose Feast Predicts the Weather

name: St. Ephrem the Syrian
facts: Deacon and Doctor of the Church called the Harp of the Holy Spirit
Wrote hundreds of hymns and poems defending orthodoxy against heresy
Introduced sung homilies that shaped Eastern liturgical tradition
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1920 by Pope Benedict XV
titleHook: Harp of the Holy Spirit and Doctor of the Church

name: St. Getulius and Companions
facts: Roman martyrs who suffered under Emperor Hadrian
Getulius was a magistrate who converted and was killed with his family
Their relics were translated to the cathedral of Amelia in Umbria
Venerated since the early centuries of the Roman Church
titleHook: Magistrate Martyr of the Early Church

name: St. Barnabas the Apostle
facts: Levite from Cyprus who sold land and gave proceeds to the apostles
Introduced Paul to the apostles in Jerusalem after his conversion
His name means son of encouragement in Aramaic
Patron of Cyprus where his tomb was discovered in 488
titleHook: Son of Encouragement and Apostle to Cyprus

name: St. John of Sahagún
facts: Augustinian friar and preacher who reformed clergy in León
Known for gentle but effective preaching that converted sinners
Refused bishoprics to remain a simple preacher
Canonized in 1690 as a model of priestly holiness
titleHook: Augustinian Preacher Who Reformed León

name: St. Anthony of Padua
facts: Franciscan preacher and Doctor of the Church called the Hammer of Heretics
Renowned for miracles including finding lost objects and preaching to fish
His tongue is incorrupt in Padua as a sign of his eloquent preaching
One of the most invoked saints in the Catholic world
titleHook: Hammer of Heretics and Finder of Lost Things

name: St. Eliseus the Prophet
facts: Successor to the prophet Elijah who received a double portion of his spirit
Performed miracles including healing Naaman's leprosy and raising the dead
Anointed Jehu king and prophesied throughout Israel
His story is told in the First and Second Books of Kings
titleHook: Prophet Successor to Elijah

name: St. Vitus
facts: Young martyr venerated since the early Church in Sicily
St. Vitus Dance (Sydenham's chorea) was named after devotion to him
One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers of medieval Europe
Patron invoked against epilepsy, nervous disorders, and animal bites
titleHook: Martyr Patron of Dancers and Epileptics

name: St. Lutgardis of Aywières
facts: Cistercian nun who received stigmata and visions of the Sacred Heart
One of the first mystics to receive visions of Christ's heart
Blind for the last eleven years of her life yet continued contemplative prayer
Her visions influenced later Sacred Heart devotion
titleHook: Mystic Who Saw the Sacred Heart

name: St. Emily de Vialar
facts: Founded the Sisters of St. Joseph of the Apparition
Established missions in Algeria, Malta, and the Middle East
Used her inheritance to fund schools and hospitals for the poor
Canonized in 1951 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Founder Who Built Missions Across Three Continents

name: St. Elizabeth of Schönau
facts: Benedictine nun who received visions of the Passion and the Virgin Mary
Her visions of the Virgin Mary's life influenced medieval Marian devotion
Corresponded with St. Hildegard of Bingen and Church leaders
Her writings were widely read throughout medieval Europe
titleHook: Benedictine Mystic and Visionary

name: St. Romuald
facts: Founder of the Camaldolese order combining eremitic and communal life
Converted after witnessing his father kill a man in a duel
Reformed monasteries across Italy and sent missionaries to Hungary
His rule balances solitude and community in monastic life
titleHook: Founder of the Camaldolese Order

name: St. Silverius
facts: Pope exiled by Empress Theodora for refusing to restore a heretical bishop
Sent to the island of Palmaria where he died of starvation and mistreatment
Venerated as a martyr for defending Church discipline
His tomb at Ponza island became a pilgrimage site
titleHook: Pope Martyr Exiled for Defending Orthodoxy

name: St. Aloysius Gonzaga
facts: Jesuit scholastic who died at twenty-three caring for plague victims
Renounced a marquisate and military career to join the Society of Jesus
Patron of youth and students since declared by Pope Benedict XIII
His innocence and purity are held up as a model for young Catholics
titleHook: Patron of Youth Who Died Serving Plague Victims

name: Sts. Thomas More and John Fisher
facts: Both martyred by Henry VIII for refusing to accept royal supremacy over the Church
Thomas More was Lord Chancellor; John Fisher was Bishop of Rochester
Canonized together in 1935 by Pope Pius XI
Patrons of lawyers, politicians, and statesmen since 2000
titleHook: Martyrs Who Defied Henry VIII

name: St. Joseph Cafasso
facts: Priest of Turin known as the Priest of the Gallows for his prison ministry
Spiritual director of St. John Bosco and model for the Salesian charism
Converted condemned prisoners through patient spiritual direction
Canonized in 1947 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Priest of the Gallows of Turin

name: St. John the Baptist
facts: Forerunner of Christ who baptized Jesus in the Jordan River
Preached repentance in the wilderness and prepared the way of the Lord
Beheaded by Herod Antipas at the request of Salome
Only saint besides Mary whose birth and death are both celebrated
titleHook: Forerunner Who Baptized Christ in the Jordan

name: St. William of Montevergine
facts: Founder of the Monte Vergine congregation of Benedictine monks
Pilgrim who walked barefoot to Santiago, Rome, and Jerusalem
His monastery on Monte Vergine still houses a famous Black Madonna
Known for miracles and strict asceticism throughout southern Italy
titleHook: Founder of Monte Vergine Abbey

name: St. Josemaría Escrivá
facts: Founded Opus Dei to sanctify ordinary work and daily life
Taught that all faithful can become saints through their everyday duties
Canonized in 2002 by Pope John Paul II
His writings on the universal call to holiness influenced Vatican II
titleHook: Founder Who Taught Sanctity in Daily Work

name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
facts: Patriarch of Alexandria and champion of Mary as Theotokos at Ephesus
Doctor of the Church who defended orthodoxy against Nestorianism
His Christological writings shaped the Council of Chalcedon
One of the most important theologians of the early Church
titleHook: Champion of Mary as Mother of God

name: St. Irenaeus of Lyon
facts: Bishop of Lyon and earliest systematic theologian of the Church
Wrote Against Heresies defending apostolic tradition against Gnosticism
Disciple of St. Polycarp who knew St. John the Apostle
Declared Doctor of the Church in 2022 by Pope Francis
titleHook: First Great Theologian Against Gnosticism

name: Sts. Peter and Paul
facts: Chief apostle and apostle to the Gentiles, pillars of the early Church
Both martyred in Rome under Nero around the mid-first century
Their joint feast celebrates the unity of Jewish and Gentile Christianity
Major solemnity with obligatory attendance in the Catholic Church
titleHook: Pillars of the Church Martyred in Rome

name: First Martyrs of the Church of Rome
facts: Christians martyred under Emperor Nero after the Great Fire of Rome
Nero blamed Christians for the fire and ordered brutal executions
Included crucifixions and burning alive as human torches
Their blood made the Church of Rome a seed of future saints
titleHook: Martyrs Under Nero After the Great Fire

name: St. Junipero Serra
facts: Franciscan friar who founded nine missions in California
Baptized over six thousand Native Americans along El Camino Real
Canonized in 2015 by Pope Francis on U.S. soil
His missions shaped the cultural landscape of California
titleHook: Franciscan Who Founded California's Missions

name: St. Bernardino Realino
facts: Jesuit priest who served as pastor of Lecce for forty-two years
Known as the Apostle of Lecce for his tireless pastoral work
Experienced mystical visions and bilocation during his ministry
Canonized in 1947 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Apostle of Lecce for Forty-Two Years

name: St. Thomas the Apostle
facts: Apostle who doubted the Resurrection until he touched Christ's wounds
Tradition holds he evangelized India and was martyred at Mylapore
The St. Thomas Christians of Kerala trace their origins to his mission
His feast celebrates faith that moves from doubt to proclamation
titleHook: Apostle Who Brought the Gospel to India

name: St. Elizabeth of Portugal
facts: Queen of Portugal known as the Peacemaker for reconciling warring factions
Sold her jewels to feed famine victims and founded hospitals
Lived as a Franciscan tertiary after her husband's death
Patroness of Portugal; canonized in 1625
titleHook: Queen Peacemaker of Portugal

name: St. Anthony Mary Zaccaria
facts: Founder of the Barnabites to reform clergy and laity in Milan
Pioneer of forty-hour Eucharistic adoration devotions
Physician who gave up medicine to become a priest
Canonized in 1897 for his reforming zeal
titleHook: Founder of the Barnabites and Eucharistic Adoration

name: St. Maria Goretti
facts: Martyred at age eleven for resisting sexual assault
Forgave her attacker Alessandro on her deathbed
Alessandro later repented and attended her canonization in 1950
Patroness of youth and victims of sexual violence
titleHook: Child Martyr Who Forgave Her Killer

name: St. Willibald
facts: English bishop who made the first recorded pilgrimage from England to Rome and the Holy Land
Brother of St. Walburga and uncle of St. Boniface
First Bishop of Eichstätt in Bavaria
His travel account is the earliest English travel writing
titleHook: First English Pilgrim to the Holy Land

name: St. Grimbald of Winchester
facts: Benedictine monk invited by King Alfred to reform English monasticism
Helped establish the Benedictine revival in Anglo-Saxon England
Became abbot of the New Minster at Winchester
His reforms shaped English monastic life for centuries
titleHook: Monk Who Reformed English Benedictine Life

name: St. Augustine Zhao Rong and Companions
facts: Chinese martyrs who died during persecution from 1648 to 1930
Augustine Zhao Rong was a soldier who became a diocesan priest
Group of 120 martyrs canonized together in 2000
Represents four centuries of Chinese Catholic witness
titleHook: Chinese Martyrs Who Witnessed for Four Centuries

name: St. Veronica Giuliani
facts: Capuchin abbess who bore the stigmata for over fifty years
Her spiritual diary spans over twenty-two thousand pages
Experienced mystical marriage and visions of the Passion
Canonized in 1839 by Pope Gregory XVI
titleHook: Stigmatic Abbess of the Capuchin Order

name: St. Benedict of Nursia
facts: Father of Western monasticism and author of the Benedictine Rule
Founded Monte Cassino, the mother abbey of Western monasticism
Patron of Europe alongside Sts. Cyril and Methodius and St. Teresa Benedicta
His rule of ora et labora shaped civilization for fifteen centuries
titleHook: Father of Western Monasticism

name: St. John Gualbert
facts: Founder of the Vallombrosan Benedictine congregation
Forgave his brother's murderer, inspiring his conversion to monastic life
Known for reforming clergy and protecting the poor in Tuscany
Patron of forests and the Vallombrosan order
titleHook: Founder Who Forgave His Brother's Murderer

name: St. Henry II
facts: Holy Roman Emperor who supported Church reform and monasticism
Founded the Diocese of Bamberg and its magnificent cathedral
Lived in partnership with his wife St. Cunegund in chastity
Patron of the childless and Benedictine oblates
titleHook: Emperor Who Founded the Diocese of Bamberg

name: St. Camillus de Lellis
facts: Founder of the Camillians, the first religious order dedicated to the sick
Former soldier and gambler who reformed after a leg wound
His red cross inspired the modern Red Cross symbol
Patron of nurses, hospitals, and the sick; canonized in 1746
titleHook: Founder of the Ministers of the Infirm

name: St. Bonaventure
facts: Franciscan theologian and Doctor of the Church called the Seraphic Doctor
General of the Franciscan order who defended its charism at councils
Wrote The Mind's Journey to God, a classic of mystical theology
Cardinal Bishop of Albano; died at the Council of Lyon in 1274
titleHook: Seraphic Doctor of the Franciscan Order

name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel
facts: Title honoring Mary as patroness of the Carmelite order
Tradition holds she gave the brown scapular to St. Simon Stock in 1251
Mount Carmel in Palestine is where Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal
Scapular devotion spread worldwide as a sign of Marian consecration
titleHook: Patroness of the Carmelites and Scapular Devotion

name: St. Leo IV
facts: Pope who rebuilt Rome's walls after Saracen raids in 846
The Leonine City walls he built still bear his name
Crowned Louis II as Holy Roman Emperor in 850
Known for charity to the poor and rebuilding churches
titleHook: Pope Who Rebuilt Rome's Walls

name: St. Frederick of Utrecht
facts: Bishop of Utrecht murdered for reforming clergy and condemning immorality
His reforms threatened powerful families who arranged his assassination
Patron of the Netherlands and model of episcopal courage
His martyrdom strengthened the Church in the Low Countries
titleHook: Bishop Martyr Who Reformed the Low Countries

name: St. Macrina the Younger
facts: Older sister of Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory of Nyssa
Founded a community of women on the family estate in Pontus
Her brother Gregory wrote her biography as a model of Christian philosophy
Called the Teacher for her spiritual wisdom and guidance
titleHook: Teacher Who Shaped the Cappadocian Fathers

name: St. Apollinaris of Ravenna
facts: First Bishop of Ravenna, sent by St. Peter according to tradition
Evangelized Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy
Martyred during persecution; his basilica in Ravenna is a UNESCO site
Patron of Ravenna and invoked against gout
titleHook: First Bishop and Martyr of Ravenna

name: St. Lawrence of Brindisi
facts: Capuchin friar and Doctor of the Church who spoke seven languages
Preached crusade and led Christian forces to victory at Székesfehérvár
Wrote extensive commentaries on Scripture in multiple languages
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1959 by Pope John XXIII
titleHook: Capuchin Doctor Who Spoke Seven Languages

name: St. Mary Magdalene
facts: First witness of the Resurrection; the Apostle to the Apostles
Jesus cast seven demons from her; she became his devoted follower
Present at the Crucifixion and the empty tomb on Easter morning
Her feast was elevated to a feast day in 2016 by Pope Francis
titleHook: Apostle to the Apostles and First Witness of the Resurrection

name: St. Bridget of Sweden
facts: Founder of the Bridgettine order and patroness of Europe
Received visions of Christ's Passion recorded in her Revelations
Made pilgrimages to Rome, Santiago, and the Holy Land
Canonized in 1391; one of the most influential medieval mystics
titleHook: Mystic Foundress and Patroness of Europe

name: St. Christina the Astonishing
facts: Known for extraordinary mystical experiences including apparent death and resurrection
Lived in extreme austerity and prayer after recovering from a seizure
Her life challenges categories of sanctity and mental experience
Venerated in Belgium for her radical devotion to Christ
titleHook: Mystic Known as the Astonishing

name: St. James the Apostle
facts: First apostle martyred; beheaded by Herod Agrippa I in Jerusalem
Patron of Spain where his shrine at Santiago de Compostela draws millions
Son of Zebedee and brother of St. John the Evangelist
The Camino de Santiago is one of the world's greatest pilgrimages
titleHook: Apostle and Patron of Spain and Pilgrims

name: Sts. Anne and Joachim
facts: Traditionally the parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Their names come from the Protoevangelium of James, an early Christian text
Patrons of grandparents and those struggling with infertility
Their feast celebrates the holy lineage leading to Christ
titleHook: Parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary

name: St. Pantaleon
facts: Physician martyred under Diocletian for treating Christian prisoners free
One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers venerated in medieval Europe
Patron of physicians and lottery players in popular devotion
His name means all-compassionate in Greek
titleHook: Physician Martyr of the Fourteen Holy Helpers

name: St. Innocent I
facts: Pope who asserted Roman primacy over the entire Church
Confirmed the canonical books of Scripture for the Western Church
Defended St. John Chrysostom against unjust condemnation
His decretals shaped early canon law development
titleHook: Pope Who Defined the Biblical Canon

name: St. Martha
facts: Sister of Lazarus and Mary; hosted Jesus in her home at Bethany
Declared by Jesus that she chose the better part by listening at his feet
Tradition holds she evangelized Provence in France after Christ's ascension
Patroness of cooks, homemakers, and those who serve others
titleHook: Disciple Who Served Christ in Bethany

name: St. Peter Chrysologus
facts: Archbishop of Ravenna called Golden-Worded for his eloquent preaching
Wrote over 170 short, powerful sermons still studied today
Defended the Incarnation against Eutychianism at the Council of Chalcedon
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1729 by Pope Benedict XIII
titleHook: Golden-Worded Doctor of Ravenna

name: St. Ignatius of Loyola
facts: Founder of the Society of Jesus (Jesuits)
Wrote the Spiritual Exercises, a cornerstone of Catholic spirituality
Converted after being wounded at the Battle of Pamplona in 1521
His order became the largest male religious order in the Church
titleHook: Founder of the Jesuits and Author of the Spiritual Exercises

name: St. Alphonsus Liguori
facts: Founder of the Redemptorists and Doctor of the Church
Wrote The Glories of Mary and thousands of works on moral theology
Bishop of Sant'Agata de' Goti who lived in extreme poverty
Patron of confessors and moral theologians since 1950
titleHook: Doctor of Moral Theology and Founder of the Redemptorists

name: St. Eusebius of Vercelli
facts: Bishop exiled for refusing to sign Arian condemnation of St. Athanasius
Introduced communal life for cathedral clergy in the West
His steadfastness helped preserve Nicene orthodoxy in Italy
Venerated as a model bishop who suffered for the faith
titleHook: Bishop Exiled for Defending Athanasius

name: St. Lydia of Philippi
facts: First European convert to Christianity baptized by St. Paul
Successful businesswoman who dealt in purple cloth
Her home in Philippi became the meeting place for the first European church
Named in Acts 16:14–15 as a woman of open heart
titleHook: First European Convert to Christianity

name: St. John Vianney
facts: Curé of Ars who spent up to seventeen hours daily in the confessional
Patron of parish priests worldwide since 1929
Performed miracles of healing, bilocation, and reading souls
Canonized in 1925; his incorrupt body is venerated at Ars
titleHook: Curé of Ars and Patron of Parish Priests

name: St. Oswald of Northumbria
facts: Christian king of Northumbria who united his kingdom under the faith
Died in battle against the pagan King Penda at Maserfield
His severed arm remained incorrupt and was venerated as a relic
Bede's Ecclesiastical History celebrates his piety and charity
titleHook: Christian King Martyr of Northumbria

name: Transfiguration of the Lord
facts: Jesus revealed his divine glory to Peter, James, and John on Mount Tabor
Moses and Elijah appeared speaking with Christ about his coming Passion
The Father's voice declared: This is my beloved Son; listen to him
Feast established to commemorate victory over Islam at Belgrade in 1456
titleHook: Feast of Christ's Glory Revealed on Mount Tabor

name: St. Cajetan of Thiene
facts: Founder of the Theatines to reform clergy and serve the poor
Established pawn shops (montes pietatis) to combat usury
Patron of job seekers and the unemployed
Canonized in 1671 for his work among the urban poor
titleHook: Founder of the Theatines and Patron of Job Seekers

name: St. Dominic de Guzmán
facts: Founder of the Order of Preachers (Dominicans)
Preached against the Albigensian heresy in southern France
Received the Rosary from the Blessed Virgin according to tradition
His order produced more saints and scholars than any other
titleHook: Founder of the Dominicans and the Rosary

name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
facts: Born Edith Stein; Jewish philosopher who converted and became a Carmelite nun
Martyred at Auschwitz during the Nazi persecution of Jews and Catholics
Co-patroness of Europe alongside Cyril, Methodius, and Benedict
Canonized in 1998 by Pope John Paul II
titleHook: Philosopher Martyr of Auschwitz

name: St. Lawrence of Rome
facts: Deacon martyred under Valerian; roasted on a gridiron according to tradition
When asked to hand over Church treasures he presented the poor
One of the most venerated martyrs of the early Roman Church
His feast coincides with the Perseid meteor shower called the Tears of St. Lawrence
titleHook: Deacon Martyr Who Presented the Poor as Treasure

name: St. Clare of Assisi
facts: Founder of the Poor Clares; first woman to write a monastic rule
Turned away an army by displaying the Blessed Sacrament at her convent
Lived in extreme poverty and contemplative prayer for forty-one years
Patroness of television for receiving Mass visions when too ill to attend
titleHook: Founder of the Poor Clares and Defender of Assisi

name: St. Jane Frances de Chantal
facts: Co-founded the Visitation order with St. Francis de Sales
Widowed at twenty-eight with four children before entering religious life
Established eighty-six Visitation convents across France
Known for gentle spirituality and care for the forgotten poor
titleHook: Co-Founder of the Visitation Order

name: Sts. Pontian and Hippolytus
facts: Pope and antipope who reconciled before dying together in Sardinian mines
Both exiled by Emperor Maximinus Thrax during persecution
Their joint feast celebrates reconciliation in the Church
Hippolytus was once a rigorist opponent of papal authority
titleHook: Pope and Antipope Reconciled in Martyrdom

name: St. Maximilian Kolbe
facts: Franciscan friar who volunteered to die in place of a stranger at Auschwitz
Founded the Militia Immaculatae and published Knight of the Immaculata magazine
Starved for two weeks before being killed with a lethal injection
Canonized in 1982 by Pope John Paul II as a martyr of charity
titleHook: Martyr of Charity at Auschwitz

name: Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
facts: Mary was taken body and soul into heavenly glory at the end of her earthly life
Defined as dogma by Pope Pius XII in 1950
Ancient feast celebrated in both East and West since the early centuries
Foreshadows the resurrection of all believers at the end of time
titleHook: Feast of Mary's Bodily Assumption into Heaven

name: St. Stephen of Hungary
facts: First Christian king of Hungary who united the nation under the faith
Founded the Archdiocese of Esztergom and numerous monasteries
His crown became the sacred symbol of Hungarian nationhood
Canonized in 1083; patron saint of Hungary
titleHook: First Christian King and Patron of Hungary

name: St. Hyacinth of Poland
facts: Dominican missionary called the Apostle of the North
Preached across Poland, Prussia, Lithuania, and Scandinavia
Legend says he saved the Blessed Sacrament from invading Mongols
Patron of Poland alongside St. Stanislaus and St. Adalbert
titleHook: Apostle of the North and Dominican Missionary

name: St. Helena
facts: Empress mother of Constantine who discovered the True Cross in Jerusalem
Built churches at Bethlehem, the Mount of Olives, and Golgotha
Patroness of archaeologists and those in difficult marriages
Venerated in both East and West for her pilgrimage to the Holy Land
titleHook: Empress Who Found the True Cross

name: St. John Eudes
facts: Promoted devotion to the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary
Founded the Eudists and the Sisters of Our Lady of Charity
Wrote the first official liturgy for the Sacred Heart devotion
Canonized in 1925 for shaping modern Catholic devotions
titleHook: Apostle of the Sacred and Immaculate Hearts

name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
facts: Cistercian abbot and Doctor of the Church called the Mellifluous Doctor
Preached the Second Crusade and defended the faith against Abelard
Wrote extensively on love; his hymns include Jesu Dulcis Memoria
One of the most influential figures of the twelfth century
titleHook: Mellifluous Doctor of Cistercian Spirituality

name: St. Pius X
facts: Pope who lowered the age of First Communion to the age of reason
Reformed Church music by promoting Gregorian chant
Opposed modernism and encouraged frequent reception of the Eucharist
Canonized in 1954; first pope saint since Pius V
titleHook: Pope Who Lowered the Age of First Communion

name: Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary
facts: Celebrates Mary as Queen of Heaven and Earth
Instituted by Pope Pius XII in 1954 following the Assumption dogma
Mary's queenship flows from her role as Mother of God
Ancient title Queen of Heaven found in Scripture and tradition
titleHook: Feast of Mary as Queen of Heaven and Earth

name: St. Rose of Lima
facts: First person born in the Americas to be canonized a saint
Dominican tertiary who lived in extreme penance and prayer in Lima
Patroness of Peru, Latin America, and the Philippines
Canonized in 1671 by Pope Clement X
titleHook: First Saint Born in the Americas

name: St. Bartholomew the Apostle
facts: Apostle also identified as Nathanael in the Gospel of John
Tradition holds he evangelized Armenia and was flayed alive
Michelangelo depicted his martyrdom in the Sistine Chapel
Patron of Armenia where the Armenian Apostolic Church honors him
titleHook: Apostle Who Evangelized Armenia

name: St. Louis IX of France
facts: King of France who led two crusades and established fair justice
Built Sainte-Chapelle to house Christ's Crown of Thorns
Patron of France alongside St. Joan of Arc and St. Denis
Canonized in 1297; model of a Christian monarch
titleHook: Crusader King and Patron of France

name: St. Elizabeth Bichier des Ages
facts: Co-founded the Daughters of the Cross with St. Andrew Fournet
Reopened schools and cared for the poor after the French Revolution
Her congregation spread education across France and Belgium
Canonized in 1947 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Founder Who Rebuilt Catholic Education After the Revolution

name: St. Monica
facts: Mother of St. Augustine; prayed for his conversion for seventeen years
Followed him from Africa to Milan seeking his spiritual welfare
Patroness of wives, mothers, and victims of abuse
Her tears and prayers are credited with Augustine's conversion
titleHook: Mother Whose Prayers Converted St. Augustine

name: St. Augustine of Hippo
facts: Bishop of Hippo and one of the greatest Doctors of the Church
Wrote Confessions and City of God, shaping all Western theology
Converted through the preaching of St. Ambrose and his mother Monica
His theology of grace remains foundational to Catholic thought
titleHook: Doctor of Grace and Bishop of Hippo

name: Beheading of St. John the Baptist
facts: Commemorates the martyrdom of John the Baptist by Herod Antipas
Salome's dance led Herod to order John's beheading despite his regret
