One of the oldest feasts in the Christian calendar
Relics of his head and body are venerated in multiple churches
titleHook: Memorial of the Forerunner's Martyrdom

name: St. Fiacre
facts: Irish monk who founded a hospice and garden at Meaux in France
Patron of gardeners and herbalists for his healing herb garden
Pilgrims sought his intercession for healing at his shrine
His name became associated with Parisian cab stands (fiacres)
titleHook: Irish Monk Patron of Gardeners

name: St. Raymond Nonnatus
facts: Mercedarian friar who ransomed Christians from Moorish captivity
Legend says his mouth was padlocked when he continued preaching in captivity
Patron of childbirth, midwives, and those suffering from gossip
His title Nonnatus means not born, as he was delivered by Caesarean section
titleHook: Mercedarian Who Was Padlocked for Preaching

name: St. Giles of Assisi
facts: Hermit who lived in a forest near Nîmes in southern France
King Wamba of Spain built a monastery at his hermitage
Patron of the disabled, lepers, and those with physical ailments
One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers of medieval devotion
titleHook: Hermit Patron of the Disabled

name: St. Ingrid of Skänninge
facts: Dominican nun who founded the first Dominican convent in Sweden
Known for visions and strict observance of religious life
Her convent at Skänninge became a center of Swedish spirituality
Represents the spread of monasticism to medieval Scandinavia
titleHook: Founder of Sweden's First Dominican Convent

name: St. Gregory the Great
facts: Pope and Doctor of the Church who sent missionaries to England
Reformed liturgy; Gregorian chant bears his name
Wrote Pastoral Care, the standard manual for bishops for centuries
Last pope universally recognized as a Father of the Church
titleHook: Pope Who Sent Missionaries to England

name: St. Rosalia of Palermo
facts: Hermit who lived in a cave on Monte Pellegrino above Palermo
Her relics discovered in 1624 ended a plague in Palermo
Patroness of Palermo; her feast draws massive celebrations in Sicily
Procession of her relics through Palermo is one of Italy's greatest
titleHook: Hermit Whose Relics Ended a Plague in Palermo

name: St. Teresa of Calcutta
facts: Founded the Missionaries of Charity serving the poorest of the poor
Nobel Peace Prize winner who lived in radical solidarity with the dying
Canonized in 2016 by Pope Francis on the Feast of St. Peter Claver eve
Her dark night of the soul revealed deep faith amid spiritual dryness
titleHook: Saint of the Poorest of the Poor

name: St. Zachary
facts: Pope who protected Rome from Lombard invasions through diplomacy
Crowned Pepin the Short as King of the Franks, shaping medieval Europe
Known for charity to the poor and restoring churches
Last pope whose epitaph was written in Greek and Latin
titleHook: Pope Who Crowned the First Carolingian King

name: St. Cloud of France
facts: Grandson of Clovis who became a hermit priest near Paris
Gave up royal privileges to live in prayer and solitude
The city of Saint-Cloud near Paris bears his name
Patron of diocesan priests in France
titleHook: Royal Prince Who Became a Hermit Priest

name: Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
facts: Celebrates the birth of the Blessed Virgin Mary nine months after Immaculate Conception
One of the oldest Marian feasts, dating to the sixth century in the East
Mary's birth prepared salvation history for the Incarnation
Processions and celebrations mark this feast worldwide
titleHook: Feast of the Birth of the Blessed Virgin

name: St. Peter Claver
facts: Jesuit who ministered to over 300,000 African slaves in Cartagena
Called himself slave of the slaves forever
Baptized and catechized captives in the holds of slave ships
Canonized in 1888; patron of missions to African peoples and human rights
titleHook: Apostle to the Enslaved of Cartagena

name: St. Nicholas of Tolentino
facts: Augustinian friar known for visions of souls in purgatory
Patron of souls in purgatory for his intercession on their behalf
Legend says he revived a dead bird and multiplied bread for the poor
Canonized in 1446; widely venerated in Italy and the Philippines
titleHook: Patron of Souls in Purgatory

name: St. Paphnutius the Confessor
facts: Desert father and bishop who defended clerical celibacy at Nicaea
Survived torture and blinding under Maximinus without renouncing faith
His testimony at the Council of Nicaea preserved optional celibacy for clergy
Respected by both Eastern and Western Church traditions
titleHook: Desert Bishop Who Defended Clerical Celibacy

name: St. Ailbhe of Emly
facts: First bishop of Emly in County Tipperary
Evangelized the Éoganacht peoples of Munster in southern Ireland
One of the pre-Patrician saints of the Irish Church
His see at Emly was an important ecclesiastical center
titleHook: First Bishop of Emly in Ireland

name: St. John Chrysostom
facts: Patriarch of Constantinople and Doctor of the Church called Golden-Mouthed
His homilies on Scripture remain among the greatest ever preached
Exiled twice for denouncing luxury and corruption in the imperial court
Patron of preachers; his Divine Liturgy is used in Eastern churches
titleHook: Golden-Mouthed Doctor of Preaching

name: Exaltation of the Holy Cross
facts: Commemorates the discovery of the True Cross by St. Helena in 326
Also marks the recovery of the Cross from Persian captivity in 629
One of the twelve great feasts of the Eastern Orthodox Church
The cross is venerated as the instrument of humanity's salvation
titleHook: Feast of the Triumph of the Cross

name: Our Lady of Sorrows
facts: Honors the seven sorrows of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Devotion promoted by the Servite order since the thirteenth century
Mary stood at the foot of the Cross sharing in Christ's suffering
Feast connects Marian devotion to the Passion of Christ
titleHook: Memorial of Mary's Seven Sorrows at the Cross

name: Sts. Cornelius and Cyprian
facts: Pope Cornelius defended the Church against Novatian rigorism
Bishop Cyprian of Carthage wrote extensively on Church unity and the episcopate
Both martyred during Decian and Valerian persecutions
Their correspondence shaped early Catholic ecclesiology
titleHook: Pope and Bishop Martyrs of Church Unity

name: St. Hildegard of Bingen
facts: Benedictine abbess, composer, and Doctor of the Church
Wrote theological, medical, and natural science works in Latin
Received visions from age three; recorded in Scivias and Liber Divinorum Operum
Declared Doctor of the Church in 2012 by Pope Benedict XVI
titleHook: Doctor of the Church and Medieval Polymath

name: St. Joseph of Cupertino
facts: Franciscan friar known for ecstatic levitations during Mass
Patron of aviators and students taking exams
Over seventy episodes of levitation were documented by witnesses
Canonized in 1767; one of the most extraordinary mystics in Church history
titleHook: Flying Friar Patron of Aviators

name: St. Januarius
facts: Bishop of Benevento martyred during Diocletian persecution
His blood liquefies miraculously three times yearly in Naples cathedral
Patron of Naples; invoked against volcanic eruptions of Mount Vesuvius
One of the most famous ongoing miracles in the Catholic Church
titleHook: Bishop Whose Blood Liquefies in Naples

name: Sts. Eustace and Companions
facts: Roman general who converted after seeing a crucifix between a stag's antlers
Martyred with his wife and two sons under Emperor Hadrian
Patron of hunters and Madrid
His legend inspired medieval art and devotion across Europe
titleHook: General Converted by a Vision of the Cross

name: St. Matthew the Apostle
facts: Tax collector called by Jesus at his customs booth in Capernaum
Author of the first Gospel emphasizing Jesus as fulfillment of the Old Testament
Left everything to follow Christ immediately upon being called
Patron of bankers, accountants, and tax collectors
titleHook: Tax Collector Who Wrote the First Gospel

name: St. Maurice and the Theban Legion
facts: Roman legion of Christian soldiers martyred for refusing to kill civilians
Maurice led over six thousand soldiers who chose death over disobeying conscience
Patron of the Swiss Guard and infantry soldiers
Their martyrdom at Agaunum shaped Swiss Christian identity
titleHook: Soldier Martyrs Who Refused to Kill

name: St. Padre Pio of Pietrelcina
facts: Capuchin friar who bore the stigmata for fifty years
Heard confessions for up to sixteen hours daily at San Giovanni Rotondo
Founded the Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza hospital in 1956
Canonized in 2002; one of the most popular saints of the twentieth century
titleHook: Stigmatic Friar Who Bore the Wounds of Christ

name: St. Gerard Majella
facts: Redemptorist lay brother who died at age twenty-nine
Patron of expectant mothers after a miraculous cloth aided a difficult childbirth
Known for bilocation, reading hearts, and multiplying bread for the poor
Canonized in 1904 as the first saint of the Redemptorist order
titleHook: Patron of Expectant Mothers

name: St. Finbar of Cork
facts: First Bishop of Cork who founded a monastery and school
The city of Cork takes its name from his monastery
Associated with the evangelization of southern Ireland
Patron of the Diocese of Cork and Ross
titleHook: First Bishop and Patron of Cork

name: Sts. Cosmas and Damian
facts: Twin brother physicians who treated patients free of charge
Martyred during Diocletian persecution for their Christian faith
Patrons of physicians, surgeons, and pharmacists
Their basilica in Rome was a major pilgrimage site
titleHook: Twin Physician Martyrs and Patrons of Doctors

name: St. Vincent de Paul
facts: Founded the Vincentians and the Daughters of Charity
Organized relief for war refugees, orphans, and galley slaves
Patron of all charitable works; his societies serve worldwide
Canonized in 1737; transformed Catholic social charity
titleHook: Apostle of Charity Who Founded the Vincentians

name: St. Wenceslaus of Bohemia
facts: Duke of Bohemia murdered by his brother Boleslav for his Christian faith
Subject of the Christmas carol Good King Wenceslaus
Patron of the Czech Republic and Bohemia
His relics are venerated at St. Vitus Cathedral in Prague
titleHook: Good King Wenceslaus and Patron of Bohemia

name: Sts. Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael
facts: Archangels who serve God as messengers, protectors, and healers
Michael defeats Satan; Gabriel announces the Incarnation to Mary
Raphael guides Tobias and heals the blind in the Old Testament
Only angels named in Scripture; feast of the three archangels
titleHook: Feast of the Three Archangels

name: St. Jerome
facts: Translated the Bible into Latin (the Vulgate), used for over a millennium
Doctor of the Church and greatest biblical scholar of antiquity
Lived as a hermit in Bethlehem near the cave of the Nativity
His motto: Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ
titleHook: Doctor Who Translated the Bible into Latin

name: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
facts: Carmelite nun who died at twenty-four; Doctor of the Church since 1997
Her Little Way teaches holiness through small acts of love
Wrote Story of a Soul, one of the best-selling spiritual autobiographies
Patroness of missions despite never leaving her convent
titleHook: Doctor of the Little Way of Spiritual Childhood

name: Guardian Angels
facts: Each person receives a guardian angel from God at birth
Angels are pure spirits who behold the face of the Father
Jesus said their angels always behold my heavenly Father's face
Devotion to guardian angels has been encouraged since the seventeenth century
titleHook: Memorial of Our Protecting Guardian Angels

name: St. Theodore Guerin
facts: Founded the Sisters of Providence of Saint Mary-of-the-Woods in Indiana
Established schools and orphanages across the American frontier
First saint from the state of Indiana; canonized in 2006
Her order continues educational and social ministry in the United States
titleHook: Founder Who Built Schools on the American Frontier

name: St. Francis of Assisi
facts: Founded the Franciscan order and renewed the Church through radical poverty
Received the stigmata at La Verna in 1224
Composed the Canticle of the Sun, one of the first works in Italian
Patron of ecology; Pope Francis took his name in 2013
titleHook: Founder of the Franciscans and Patron of Ecology

name: St. Faustina Kowalska
facts: Polish nun who received visions of the Divine Mercy of Jesus
Jesus asked her to paint the image of Divine Mercy with the inscription Jesus I trust in You
Her diary has sold millions of copies worldwide
Canonized in 2000; Divine Mercy Sunday established by Pope John Paul II
titleHook: Apostle of Divine Mercy

name: St. Bruno of Cologne
facts: Founder of the Carthusian order combining eremitic solitude and community
Established the Grande Chartreuse monastery in the French Alps
Declined a cardinalate to remain a simple hermit
Carthusians are known as the most contemplative order in the Church
titleHook: Founder of the Carthusian Order

name: Our Lady of the Rosary
facts: Instituted by Pope St. Pius V after the Christian victory at Lepanto in 1571
Commemorates the power of the Rosary in defeating the Ottoman fleet
Also known as Our Lady of Victory
Pope Leo XIII added the title to the Litany of Loreto
titleHook: Feast of Victory Through the Holy Rosary

name: St. Pelagia the Penitent
facts: Wealthy actress who converted and became a hermit in Jerusalem
Disguised herself as a monk on the Mount of Olives for years
Her story inspired medieval penitential literature
Patroness of actresses and penitent women
titleHook: Actress Who Became a Hermit on the Mount of Olives

name: St. Denis and Companions
facts: First Bishop of Paris martyred on Montmartre (Mount of Martyrs)
Legend says he carried his severed head preaching for six miles
Patron of France alongside Joan of Arc and Louis IX
His abbey of Saint-Denis became the burial place of French kings
titleHook: Bishop Who Carried His Head After Martyrdom

name: St. Francis Borgia
facts: Grandee of Spain who became the third Superior General of the Jesuits
Renounced the Duchy of Gandia after the death of his wife
Expanded Jesuit missions to the Americas and Asia
Canonized in 1670 for his leadership and humility
titleHook: Duke Who Became Superior General of the Jesuits

name: St. John XXIII
facts: Pope who convoked the Second Vatican Council in 1962
Known as Good Pope John for his warmth, humor, and pastoral heart
His encyclical Pacem in Terris addressed peace and human rights
Canonized alongside John Paul II in 2014 by Pope Francis
titleHook: Good Pope Who Opened Vatican II

name: St. Wilfrid of York
facts: Bishop of York who championed Roman liturgical practices over Celtic customs
Built Ripon and Hexham cathedrals in Northumbria
His synod at Whitby in 664 unified English Church practice
One of the most important bishops of Anglo-Saxon England
titleHook: Bishop Who Unified English Church Practice

name: St. Edward the Confessor
facts: Last Anglo-Saxon king of England before the Norman Conquest
Built Westminster Abbey where he is buried
Known for piety, justice, and healing miracles
Patron of England before St. George; canonized in 1161
titleHook: King Who Built Westminster Abbey

name: St. Callistus I
facts: Pope who organized the Church's first public cemeteries (catacombs of Callixtus)
Former slave who rose to the papacy through faith and leadership
Martyred during persecution under Alexander Severus
His catacombs remain a major site of early Christian art
titleHook: Pope Who Organized Rome's Catacombs

name: St. Teresa of Avila
facts: Reformed the Carmelite order and became a Doctor of the Church
Wrote The Interior Castle, a masterpiece of mystical theology
Experienced ecstasies and transverberation of the heart
Co-patroness of Spain alongside St. James the Apostle
titleHook: Doctor of Mystical Prayer and Carmelite Reform

name: St. Hedwig of Silesia
facts: Duchess of Silesia who used her wealth to build monasteries and hospitals
Lived in voluntary poverty despite her royal status
Patroness of Silesia and model of Christian queenship
Canonized in 1267; her shrine at Trzebnica draws pilgrims
titleHook: Duchess Who Gave Everything to the Poor

name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
facts: Bishop of Antioch fed to lions in Rome's Colosseum around AD 107
His seven letters en route to martyrdom are treasures of early Christianity
First writer to use the term Catholic Church
Disciple of St. John the Apostle according to tradition
titleHook: Bishop Martyr Who First Wrote Catholic Church

name: St. Luke the Evangelist
facts: Author of the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles
Physician and companion of St. Paul on missionary journeys
Tradition holds he painted the first icon of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Patron of physicians, artists, and surgeons
titleHook: Evangelist and Patron of Physicians and Artists

name: Sts. Isaac Jogues and North American Martyrs
facts: Eight Jesuit missionaries martyred evangelizing Native American peoples
Isaac Jogues was captured, tortured, and killed by Mohawk warriors
Included René Goupil, Jean de Lalande, and five others
Canonized in 1930; patron saints of the Americas and missionaries
titleHook: Jesuit Martyrs of North American Missions

name: St. Paul of the Cross
facts: Founded the Passionists to preach devotion to Christ's Passion
Received visions and stigmata during his life of prayer
Preached missions across Italy for over fifty years
Canonized in 1867; his order serves worldwide
titleHook: Founder of the Passionists

name: St. Hilarion the Great
facts: Founder of monasticism in Palestine; disciple of St. Anthony of Egypt
Lived as a hermit for decades before founding monasteries
His life was written by St. Jerome
Influenced desert spirituality across the Eastern Mediterranean
titleHook: Founder of Palestinian Monasticism

name: St. John Paul II
facts: Pope for twenty-six years who helped end communism in Eastern Europe
Canonized more saints than all previous popes combined
Established World Youth Day and the Theology of the Body
Canonized in 2014 by Pope Francis alongside John XXIII
titleHook: Pope Saint of World Youth Day

name: St. John of Capistrano
facts: Franciscan friar who preached crusade against the Ottoman invasion
Led Christian forces to victory at the Siege of Belgrade in 1456
Former lawyer and governor who became a Franciscan reformer
Mission churches across the Americas bear his name
titleHook: Franciscan Who Saved Europe at Belgrade

name: St. Anthony Mary Claret
facts: Founded the Claretians and served as Archbishop of Santiago, Cuba
Preached over ten thousand sermons and published hundreds of books
Survived fifteen assassination attempts
Patron of weavers and savings; canonized in 1950
titleHook: Archbishop Who Survived Fifteen Assassination Attempts

name: Sts. Crispin and Crispinian
facts: Brother shoemakers who evangelized Gaul while making shoes for the poor
Martyred at Soissons during Diocletian persecution
Patrons of shoemakers, leather workers, and saddlers
Shakespeare's St. Crispin's Day speech honors their feast at Agincourt
titleHook: Shoemaker Martyrs Patrons of Cobblers

name: St. Alfred the Great
facts: Anglo-Saxon king who defended England against Viking invasions
Promoted education and translated Latin works into Old English
Only English monarch called the Great
His Christian governance shaped English national identity
titleHook: Only English King Called the Great

name: St. Frumentius of Ethiopia
facts: Apostle of Ethiopia who converted the Kingdom of Axum
Became the first Bishop of Axum, ordained by St. Athanasius
His mission established one of the oldest Christian churches in Africa
Ethiopian Orthodox Church venerates him as Abba Salama
titleHook: Apostle Who Brought Christianity to Ethiopia

name: Sts. Simon and Jude
facts: Apostles who preached the Gospel together according to tradition
Jude authored the New Testament epistle of Jude
Simon is called the Zealot for his former political affiliation
Patrons of desperate causes invoked when all hope seems lost
titleHook: Apostles Patrons of Desperate Causes

name: St. Narcissus of Jerusalem
facts: Bishop of Jerusalem who served until age one hundred sixteen
Accused unjustly of a crime; cleared by miraculous test with water
Ordained St. Alexander, who succeeded him as bishop
Venerated in both Eastern and Western Church traditions
titleHook: Bishop of Jerusalem Who Served Until Age 116

name: St. Alphonsus Rodriguez
facts: Jesuit lay brother and doorkeeper at the college of Montesión in Majorca
Spiritual director of St. Peter Claver before his mission to the Americas
Known for mystical prayer despite his humble duties
Canonized in 1888 as a model of holiness in ordinary work
titleHook: Doorkeeper Who Directed St. Peter Claver

name: St. Wolfgang of Regensburg
facts: Bishop of Regensburg who lived as a monk despite episcopal duties
Built churches and schools throughout Bavaria
Known for miracles of healing and exorcism
Patron of carpenters and those suffering from paralysis
titleHook: Bishop-Monk of Regensburg

name: All Saints
facts: Honors all saints in heaven, known and unknown
Rooted in early Christian commemoration of martyrs
Vigil All Hallows Eve (Halloween) precedes this great solemnity
Reminds the faithful that universal call to holiness is achievable
titleHook: Solemnity Honoring Every Saint in Heaven

name: All Souls
facts: Commemorates all the faithful departed undergoing purification
The Church offers Masses and prayers for souls in purgatory
Rooted in monastic tradition of praying for the dead since the seventh century
Visiting cemeteries and lighting candles are traditional practices
titleHook: Memorial of the Faithful Departed

name: St. Martin de Porres
facts: Dominican lay brother of mixed African and indigenous heritage in Lima
Established an orphanage and hospital for the poor in Lima
Known for miraculous healing, bilocation, and care for animals
First black saint of the Americas; canonized in 1962
titleHook: First Black Saint of the Americas

name: St. Charles Borromeo
facts: Cardinal Archbishop of Milan who implemented Council of Trent reforms
Established seminaries for priestly formation across his diocese
Fed the hungry during plague while visiting the sick personally
Patron of bishops and catechists; canonized in 1610
titleHook: Reformer Archbishop of Milan

name: St. Elizabeth of the Trinity
facts: Carmelite nun and spiritual writer who died at age twenty-six
Known for indwelling theology — God dwelling within the soul
Corresponded with friends offering profound spiritual counsel
Beatified in 1984; canonized in 2016 by Pope Francis
titleHook: Carmelite Mystic of the Indwelling Trinity

name: St. Leonard of Noblac
facts: Frankish nobleman converted by St. Remigius who became a hermit
Patron of prisoners for his intercession on their behalf
Founded the abbey of Noblac in Aquitaine
His cult spread widely across medieval Europe
titleHook: Hermit Patron of Prisoners

name: St. Willibrord
facts: Apostle of the Frisians and first Archbishop of Utrecht
English monk who evangelized the Netherlands and Denmark
Established the diocese of Utrecht as a center of Northern European Christianity
His feast marks the evangelization of the Low Countries
titleHook: Apostle of the Netherlands

name: Blessed John Duns Scotus
facts: Franciscan philosopher called the Subtle Doctor
Defended the Immaculate Conception centuries before it was defined as dogma
His metaphysics influenced Catholic theology for centuries
Beatified in 1993 by Pope John Paul II
titleHook: Subtle Doctor Who Defended the Immaculate Conception

name: Dedication of St. John Lateran
facts: Second day of celebration for the Lateran Basilica dedication
The Lateran Palace was donated to the Church by Emperor Constantine
Popes lived at the Lateran until the fourteenth century
Annual reminder that the Church is the people, not just buildings
titleHook: Mother Church of All Christendom

name: St. Leo the Great
facts: Pope and Doctor of the Church who met Attila the Hun and turned him from Rome
His Tome defined Christological orthodoxy at the Council of Chalcedon
Only pope called the Great besides Gregory I
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1754
titleHook: Pope Who Turned Back Attila the Hun

name: St. Martin of Tours
facts: Roman soldier who cut his cloak in half for a beggar who was Christ
Bishop of Tours who evangelized rural Gaul
Patron of France and soldiers; his feast marks armistice day in Europe
One of the first non-martyr saints venerated in the West
titleHook: Soldier Who Shared His Cloak with Christ

name: St. Josaphat Kuntsevych
facts: Basilian monk martyred for promoting unity between Orthodox and Catholic Churches
Archbishop of Polotsk who restored Byzantine-Slavonic liturgy in union with Rome
Killed by a mob in Vitebsk for his efforts at reconciliation
Patron of Christian unity and the Ukrainian Church
titleHook: Martyr for East-West Church Unity

name: St. Frances Xavier Cabrini
facts: First American citizen canonized; founded the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart
Established sixty-seven institutions for immigrants in the United States
Patroness of immigrants; arrived in New York with almost no resources
Canonized in 1946 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: First American Citizen Saint and Patron of Immigrants

name: St. Lawrence O'Toole
facts: Archbishop of Dublin during the Norman invasion of Ireland
Known for fasting, prayer, and peacemaking between Irish and Normans
Canonized in 1225; his relics are venerated at Eu in Normandy
Patron of the Archdiocese of Dublin
titleHook: Archbishop of Dublin During the Norman Invasion

name: St. Albert the Great
facts: Dominican bishop and Doctor of the Church called the Universal Doctor
Teacher of St. Thomas Aquinas; pioneer of medieval science and philosophy
Wrote encyclopedic works on natural science, logic, and theology
Patron of scientists and philosophers; canonized in 1931
titleHook: Universal Doctor and Teacher of Aquinas

name: St. Margaret of Scotland
facts: Queen of Scotland who reformed the Church and promoted education
Established ferries for pilgrims and fed the hungry at her table
Patroness of Scotland; canonized in 1250
Known as the Pearl of Scotland for her piety and charity
titleHook: Pearl of Scotland and Queen of Charity

name: St. Elizabeth of Hungary
facts: Princess who became a Franciscan tertiary and served the sick and poor
Built a hospital at Marburg and personally nursed leprosy patients
Died at age twenty-four; one of the most beloved medieval saints
Patroness of bakers and the Franciscan Third Order
titleHook: Princess Who Served the Poor and Sick

name: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne
facts: Religious of the Sacred Heart who brought Catholic education to the American frontier
Established the first free school for Native American girls west of the Mississippi
Known as the Woman Who Prays Always for her constant intercession
Canonized in 1988 by Pope John Paul II
titleHook: Missionary Who Educated Native American Girls

name: St. Mechtilde of Hackeborn
facts: Benedictine nun at Helfta who received visions of the Sacred Heart
Her revelations influenced later Sacred Heart devotion
Sister of St. Gertrude the Great at the convent of Helfta
Her Book of Special Grace records her mystical experiences
titleHook: Mystic Who Saw Visions of the Sacred Heart

name: St. Edmund the Martyr
facts: Anglo-Saxon king of East Anglia martyred by Danish Vikings
Refused to renounce Christianity when captured by the Great Heathen Army
Patron of East Anglia; his shrine at Bury St. Edmunds was a major pilgrimage
His martyrdom is depicted in the Bayeux Tapestry
titleHook: Anglo-Saxon King Martyred by Vikings

name: Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
facts: Commemorates Mary being presented in the Temple as a young girl
Based on the Protoevangelium of James, an early Christian tradition
Patronal feast of the Carmelite order worldwide
Celebrates Mary's total dedication to God from childhood
titleHook: Feast of Mary's Presentation in the Temple

name: St. Cecilia
facts: Virgin martyr who sang to God in her heart during her wedding
Patroness of musicians and one of the most venerated Roman martyrs
Her church in Rome's Trastevere is one of the oldest in the city
Named in the Roman Canon of the Mass since antiquity
titleHook: Patroness of Musicians and Virgin Martyr

name: St. Clement I
facts: Fourth pope according to tradition; disciple of St. Peter
Wrote a letter to Corinth that is one of the earliest Christian documents
Martyred by being tied to an anchor and thrown into the Black Sea
Patron of mariners; his basilica in Rome dates to the fourth century
titleHook: Early Pope Martyr Tied to an Anchor

name: Sts. Andrew Dung-Lac and Vietnamese Martyrs
facts: Group of 117 martyrs killed during Vietnamese persecutions of Christians
Included bishops, priests, lay people, and a young child
Represent centuries of Catholic witness in Vietnam
Canonized together in 1988 by Pope John Paul II
titleHook: Martyrs Who Witnessed in Vietnam

name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
facts: Virgin martyr and scholar who debated fifty philosophers and converted them
Patroness of philosophers, preachers, and unmarried girls
One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers of medieval devotion
Her wheel symbol appears in art worldwide; invoked by those seeking wisdom
titleHook: Philosopher Virgin Martyr of Alexandria

name: St. Sylvester Gozzolini
facts: Founder of the Sylvestrine Benedictine congregation
Hermit who lived in a cave before founding monasteries in central Italy
His order follows a modified Benedictine rule in solitude
Canonized in 1598 for his monastic reform
titleHook: Founder of the Sylvestrine Benedictines

name: St. Virgil of Salzburg
facts: Irish missionary bishop who evangelized Bavaria and Carinthia
Appointed Bishop of Salzburg and built the first cathedral there
Defended the legitimacy of his episcopal consecration against critics
Patron of Salzburg; his legacy shaped Austrian Christianity
titleHook: Irish Missionary Bishop of Salzburg

name: St. Catherine Labouré
facts: Daughter of Charity who received visions of the Miraculous Medal in 1830
Mary appeared standing on a globe crushing the serpent's head
Over a billion Miraculous Medals have been distributed worldwide
Her incorrupt body is venerated at the Rue du Bac chapel in Paris
titleHook: Visionary of the Miraculous Medal

name: St. Saturninus of Toulouse
facts: Bishop of Toulouse martyred by being dragged by a bull through the city
One of the earliest bishops sent to evangelize Gaul
His martyrdom established Toulouse as a center of Christian faith
Patron of Toulouse and invoked against rheumatism
titleHook: Bishop Martyred by a Bull in Toulouse

name: St. Andrew the Apostle
facts: First disciple called by Jesus; brother of St. Peter
Preached in Scythia and Greece; martyred on an X-shaped cross
Patron of Scotland, Russia, and Greece
His relics in Scotland made the country a major pilgrimage destination
titleHook: First-Called Apostle and Patron of Scotland

name: St. Edmund Campion
facts: Jesuit priest martyred under Elizabeth I for celebrating Mass in England
His Brag defended Catholic loyalty to the crown while refusing schism
Hanged, drawn, and quartered at Tyburn on December 1, 1581
One of the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales canonized in 1970
titleHook: Jesuit Martyr of Elizabethan England

name: St. Bibiana
facts: Virgin martyr scourged to death under Julian the Apostate
Her church near the Lateran in Rome dates to the fifth century
Patroness of epilepsy, headaches, and single laywomen
Her name means alive in Latin, symbolizing spiritual vitality
titleHook: Virgin Martyr of Julian the Apostate

name: St. Francis Xavier
facts: Jesuit missionary who evangelized India, Japan, and Southeast Asia
Baptized over thirty thousand converts across Asia
Died on Shangchuan Island awaiting entry to mainland China
Patron of foreign missions alongside St. Thérèse of Lisieux
titleHook: Greatest Jesuit Missionary to Asia

name: St. John Damascene
facts: Last Father of the Eastern Church and Doctor of the Church
Defended icons during the Iconoclast controversy with theological brilliance
Wrote hymns still sung in Eastern liturgies today
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1890 by Pope Leo XIII
titleHook: Doctor Who Defended Sacred Icons

name: St. Sabas of Mar Saba
facts: Founded the Great Lavra of Mar Saba in the Judean wilderness
Lived as a hermit from age eight; abbot for many years
His monastery still houses monks after fifteen centuries
One of the greatest figures of Palestinian monasticism
titleHook: Founder of the Great Lavra of Mar Saba

name: St. Nicholas of Myra
facts: Bishop of Myra known for secret gift-giving and protecting children
Saved three girls from slavery by dropping gold through their window
Patron of children, sailors, and Russia; basis for Santa Claus tradition
One of the most universally beloved saints in Christian history
titleHook: Bishop Who Became the Original Santa Claus

name: St. Ambrose of Milan
facts: Bishop of Milan who baptized St. Augustine of Hippo in 387
Doctor of the Church who introduced antiphonal chanting to the West
Stood up to Emperor Theodosius after the Massacre of Thessalonica
One of the four original Western Doctors of the Church
titleHook: Bishop Who Baptized St. Augustine

name: Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary
facts: Mary was conceived without original sin in her mother Anne's womb
Defined as dogma by Pope Pius IX in 1854
Patronal feast of the United States since 1846
Nine months before the Nativity of Mary on September 8
titleHook: Dogma of Mary's Sinless Conception

name: St. Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin
facts: Aztec convert who received apparitions of Our Lady of Guadalupe in 1531
His tilma bearing Mary's image is displayed at the Basilica of Guadalupe
First indigenous American saint; canonized in 2002 by Pope John Paul II
Our Lady's words to him: Am I not here, I who am your mother?
titleHook: Visionary of Our Lady of Guadalupe

name: St. Gregory III
facts: Pope who defended veneration of sacred icons against Byzantine iconoclasm
Built oratories to saints whose images were being destroyed in the East
Sent missionaries to evangelize Germany with St. Boniface
His Syrian origin reflects the early Church's global diversity
titleHook: Syrian Pope Who Defended Sacred Images

name: St. Damasus I
facts: Pope who commissioned St. Jerome to translate the Bible into Latin
Restored Roman catacombs and recorded martyr inscriptions
Promoted veneration of martyrs and Marian devotion in Rome
His inscriptions in the catacombs preserve early Christian history
titleHook: Pope Who Commissioned the Vulgate Bible

name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
facts: Mary appeared to Juan Diego as a mestiza woman speaking Nahuatl in 1531
Her image on the tilma converted millions of indigenous people to Christianity
Patroness of Mexico, the Americas, and the unborn
Most visited Marian shrine in the world with over twenty million pilgrims yearly
titleHook: Patroness of the Americas and the Unborn

name: St. Lucy of Syracuse
facts: Virgin martyr who gouged out her eyes rather than break her vow of chastity
Patroness of the blind and those with eye disorders
Her name means light; celebrated with candles in Scandinavian countries
One of the most venerated virgin martyrs in East and West
titleHook: Virgin Martyr Whose Name Means Light

name: St. John of the Cross
facts: Carmelite reformer and Doctor of the Church
Wrote Dark Night of the Soul and Ascent of Mount Carmel
Imprisoned by his own order for nine months for reform efforts
Co-reformer with St. Teresa of Avila of the Discalced Carmelites
titleHook: Doctor of the Dark Night of the Soul

name: St. Mary di Rosa
facts: Founded the Handmaids of Charity to serve the sick in hospitals
Nursed cholera victims during epidemics in Brescia
Her sisters served on battlefields and in prisons
Canonized in 1954 by Pope Pius XII
titleHook: Founder Who Nursed Cholera Victims

name: St. Adelaide of Italy
facts: Holy Roman Empress who rebuilt churches and monasteries across Italy
Endured imprisonment and exile from political enemies
Patroness of abuse victims for her suffering at the hands of rivals
Known for charity to the poor and support of Cluniac reform
titleHook: Empress Who Rebuilt Italy's Churches

name: St. Lazarus of Bethany
facts: Friend of Jesus whom Christ raised from the dead after four days
His resurrection foreshadows the general resurrection at the end of time
Hosted Jesus in his home at Bethany with his sisters Martha and Mary
Patron of lepers and the poor in Christian tradition
titleHook: Friend Whom Jesus Raised from the Dead

name: St. Flannan of Killaloe
facts: Bishop of Killaloe in County Clare, Ireland
Son of St. Blathmac; part of a family of Irish saints
Evangelized the region around the Shannon River
His cathedral at Killaloe served the region for centuries
titleHook: Bishop of Killaloe in Ireland

name: St. Anastasius I
facts: Pope who condemned Origenism and supported St. Jerome's biblical work
Corresponded with St. Augustine and St. Jerome on theological matters
Known for simplicity and generosity to the poor
His papacy strengthened orthodoxy at the turn of the fifth century
titleHook: Pope Who Supported St. Jerome's Vulgate

name: St. Dominic of Silos
facts: Benedictine abbot who rebuilt the abbey of Silos in Castile
Known for miracles of healing and freeing prisoners
Patron of shepherds and expectant mothers in Spain
His abbey became a center of Romanesque art and monastic life
titleHook: Abbot Who Rebuilt Silos and Freed Prisoners

name: St. Peter Canisius
facts: Jesuit theologian called the Second Apostle of Germany after Boniface
Wrote the Catechism that shaped Catholic education for centuries
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1925 by Pope Pius XI
Counter-Reformation leader who reconverted much of Central Europe
titleHook: Doctor Who Wrote the Catechism of Germany

name: St. Frances Xavier Cabrini
facts: Established hospitals, schools, and orphanages for Italian immigrants in America
Traveled across continents despite a lifelong fear of water and sailing
First U.S. citizen saint; naturalized in Seattle in 1909
Died at Columbus Hospital in Chicago on December 22, 1917
titleHook: Missionary to Immigrants Who Died in Chicago

name: St. John of Kanty
facts: Polish priest and professor of theology at the University of Kraków
Gave away everything to the poor and lived in extreme simplicity
Known for gentle preaching and tireless confessor ministry
Patron of Poland and Kraków; canonized in 1767
titleHook: Polish Professor Who Gave Everything to the Poor

name: St. Adele of Pfalzel
facts: Widowed mother who founded a convent at Pfalzel near Trier
Daughter of King Dagobert II of Austrasia
Known for charity and establishing religious communities for women
Her convent became a center of prayer and education
titleHook: Widowed Queen Who Founded a Convent

name: Nativity of the Lord
facts: Celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, the Incarnation of God
Angels announced peace on earth to shepherds in the fields of Bethlehem
Wise men from the East followed a star to adore the newborn King
Central feast of the Christian calendar and holy day of obligation
titleHook: Christmas — Birth of Our Savior in Bethlehem

name: St. Stephen the Protomartyr
facts: First Christian martyr; stoned to death while praying for his killers
One of the seven deacons chosen to serve the early Church in Jerusalem
His martyrdom is recorded in Acts 7 with his vision of Christ standing
Patron of deacons and stonemasons; feast on the day after Christmas
titleHook: First Christian Martyr Stoned While Praying

name: St. John the Apostle
facts: Beloved disciple who rested on Christ's breast at the Last Supper
Author of the fourth Gospel, three epistles, and the Book of Revelation
Only apostle not martyred; tradition holds he survived boiling in oil
Patron of love, friendship, and theologians
titleHook: Beloved Disciple and Author of the Fourth Gospel

name: Holy Innocents
facts: Male children of Bethlehem killed by King Herod seeking the Christ child
Martyred for Christ though they died before knowing him
Their feast commemorates the cost of the Incarnation
Patrons of babies and children who died before baptism
titleHook: Child Martyrs of King Herod's Massacre

name: St. Thomas Becket
facts: Archbishop of Canterbury martyred in his cathedral by knights of Henry II
Defended Church rights and clerical immunity from secular courts
His shrine at Canterbury was Christendom's greatest pilgrimage until the Reformation
Canonized in 1173; Chaucer's Canterbury Tales centers on his shrine
titleHook: Archbishop Martyred in Canterbury Cathedral

name: St. Egwin of Evesham
facts: Bishop of Worcester who founded Evesham Abbey on the Avon
Made penitential pilgrimages to Rome shackled in chains
His abbey became one of the great Benedictine houses of England
Patron of Evesham and the Worcestershire region
titleHook: Bishop Who Founded Evesham Abbey

name: St. Sylvester I
facts: Pope during the reign of Constantine who received the Lateran Palace
Presided over the First Council of Nicaea in 325 through legates
His pontificate marked the transition from persecution to imperial favor
New Year's Eve is traditionally called Sylvester's Night in many countries
titleHook: Pope Who Received the Lateran from Constantine
